Quotations: Genesis 8:4 (King James Version): “And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.” | Genesis 7:4 (King James Version): “For yet seven days, and I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and every living substance that I have made will I destroy from off the face of the earth.”
licoes.c: Thinking together respects the reader: follow the chain until literality breaks.

licoes.t: A lie repeated many times — and the right to ask
licoes.r:
In Mestre Solar's words: a lie — or an unexamined story — repeated many times can become “truth” in a person's mind, rooted in the subconscious, rarely questioned. This is not an insult to believers: it is cognitive psychology.

Science names the **illusory truth effect**: repetition increases perceived truth even when people know better (Hasher, Goldstein & Toppino, 1977; Fazio et al., 2015). Nearby: processing fluency; belief perseverance; childhood repetition plus authority.

The famous saying often blamed on Goebbels is **not documented** as his — treat it as a popular, misattributed proverb.

Gently tied to the flood: many heard Genesis 6–9 from childhood as settled fact. Examining verses, physics, and Near Eastern parallels is not a duty to abandon faith — it is the right not to let fear or habit think for you. Invite: question with calm, not fear. Sincere faith can bear light.
licoes.a: Hasher et al. 1977; Fazio et al. 2015; Quote Investigator on the misattribution. Return to the Calculator and “Think together.”
licoes.c: The subconscious is a garden: what you plant by repetition, you harvest as “obvious.”

licoes.r: Portal verdict: water volume ❌; rain and latent heat ❌; fountains of the deep ❌; pressure/oxygen and salinity ❌; ark structure and logistics ❌; biogeography and pair genetics ❌; Ussher chronology vs civilizations and layered geology ❌. Local Mesopotamian floods ✅; Atrahasis/Gilgamesh/Ziusudra parallels ✅; J/P stitching ✅; Black Sea ⚠️. Overall: a literal global flood as physical reportage of Genesis 6–9 does not hold. That does not license mocking believers: many read it as theological narrative about violence, covenant, and restart, echoing real floods and older myths. Lying about Earth’s physics does not strengthen faith; honesty does.
licoes.a: Open the Flood Calculator (conteudo/calculadora-diluvio.html), vary height, rain days, and species, and watch the formulas. If your faith is literalist, this will sting—and the Portal prefers true discomfort to false comfort.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the courage to say “it doesn’t match” can be as spiritual as the courage to wait for a miracle.

licoes.r: The app includes an offline Flood Calculator in the Portal’s gray-gold theme: conteudo/calculadora-diluvio.html. Choose target height (default Everest+15 cubits), rain days, cubit, species/pairs, and food per animal. It returns water volume vs oceans, mm/h vs record, heat and ΔT, ark volume per animal, food/water/manure per day, workload, and hypothetical kangaroo travel time. Formulas shown. Labels PT/EN/ES.
licoes.a: The calculator neither “proves God” nor “destroys God.” It turns physical claims into arithmetic. Águia Primordial remains the Portal voice; this new theme has no dedicated Águia recording yet—device voice may read until audio exists.
licoes.c: To contemplate: measuring is a form of respect for reality.

licoes.t: What the Adam and Eve story tells (Genesis 1–5)
licoes.r: Genesis 1 tells of creation in six days, ending with man and woman created together (Gen 1:27: “male and female created he them”). Genesis 2 tells it again: man is formed from dust (Gen 2:7), placed in Eden, and woman is made from a rib (Gen 2:22). In Genesis 3 a talking serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (Gen 3:6); curses and expulsion follow (Gen 3:23). Genesis 4–5 continue with Cain, Abel and lifespans over 900 years. This theme does not mock faith: it checks each detail against science and against the text itself, verse in hand.
licoes.a:
How to read this theme: every claim comes with its verse quoted right there and with the scientific source. At the end there is a table of what matches, what doesn't and what can't be verified. Practice: read Genesis 1 to 5 in one go and note what is a number, what is the order of events and what is teaching.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 1:1 (King James Version, public domain): “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A1&version=KJV | Genesis 1:27 (King James Version, public domain): “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A27&version=KJV | Genesis 2:7 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A7&version=KJV | Genesis 2:22 (King James Version, public domain): “And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A22&version=KJV | Genesis 3:6 (King James Version, public domain): “And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A6&version=KJV | Genesis 3:23 (King James Version, public domain): “Therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A23&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: a story can carry meaning (responsibility, guilt, longing for a paradise) without being a lab report. Here we separate the spiritual search from physical claims that can be tested.

licoes.r: Genesis marks days with evening and morning (Gen 1:5: “And the evening and the morning were the first day”) and ends the work on the seventh day (Gen 2:2). Science measures another scale: Earth is about 4.54 billion years old, from radiometric dating of meteorites and the oldest rocks — source: https://pubs.usgs.gov/gip/geotime/age.html. The universe is about 13.8 billion years old. The sum: 6 days versus about 1.6 trillion days for Earth alone.
licoes.a:
How radiometric dating works: certain atoms (uranium, potassium) turn into others at a constant rate measured in the lab. Like an hourglass, the ratio between what is left and what formed tells how long ago the rock closed. Different methods in different labs reach the same age — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiometric_dating. Some read the 'days' as ages. Even so, the order of events doesn't match, as the next lesson shows.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 1:5 (King James Version, public domain): “And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A5&version=KJV | Genesis 1:31 (King James Version, public domain): “And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A31&version=KJV | Genesis 2:2 (King James Version, public domain): “And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A2&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: deep time doesn't shrink the mystery, it grows it.

licoes.t: The order of creation vs the fossil record
licoes.r: Genesis 1 gives an order: light on day 1 (Gen 1:3), fruit trees on day 3 (Gen 1:11), Sun and stars only on day 4 (Gen 1:16), fish, great sea creatures and birds on day 5 (Gen 1:20–21), land animals on day 6 (Gen 1:24). The fossil record shows another: the Sun (≈4.6 billion years) comes before Earth — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun; land animals (≈370 million, like Tiktaalik) come before birds (≈150 million, descended from dinosaurs) — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_of_birds; fruiting plants only ≈130 million — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowering_plant; and whales came from land mammals ≈50 million years ago — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_cetaceans.
licoes.a:
Real order, summarised: Sun → Earth → sea life (≈3.5 billion) → land plants (≈470 million) → land vertebrates (≈370 million) → dinosaurs → birds (≈150 million) → flowering plants (≈130 million) → whales (≈50 million) → Homo sapiens (≈300,000). One point matches: humans came last. The others don't.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 1:3 (King James Version, public domain): “And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A3&version=KJV | Genesis 1:11 (King James Version, public domain): “And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A11&version=KJV | Genesis 1:16 (King James Version, public domain): “And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A16&version=KJV | Genesis 1:20 (King James Version, public domain): “And God said, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A20&version=KJV | Genesis 1:21 (King James Version, public domain): “And God created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged fowl after his kind: and God saw that it was good.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A21&version=KJV | Genesis 1:24 (King James Version, public domain): “And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind: and it was so.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A24&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: the real sequence is a branching tree, not six shelves.

licoes.t: Genesis 1 vs Genesis 2: two different orders
licoes.r: Side by side. Genesis 1: plants (Gen 1:11) → animals (Gen 1:24) → man and woman together, last (Gen 1:27: “male and female created he them”). Genesis 2: no plant of the field yet (Gen 2:5) → man is formed (Gen 2:7) → God makes trees grow (Gen 2:9) → forms the animals and brings them to the man (Gen 2:19: “out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field... and brought them unto Adam”) → finally woman, from the rib (Gen 2:22). In chapter 1 man comes after the animals; in 2, before. In 1 the couple is created together; in 2, separately.
licoes.a:
Why: the most accepted scholarly explanation is that Genesis joins two accounts of different origins. Genesis 1 ('Priestly', P) uses 'God' (Elohim), orderly and solemn; Genesis 2 ('Yahwist', J) uses 'LORD God' (YHWH Elohim) and is a story with God shaping clay — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_hypothesis. Defenders of a single reading say Gen 2 only 'details' Gen 1, but the order of events is still different.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 1:11 (King James Version, public domain): “And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A11&version=KJV | Genesis 1:24 (King James Version, public domain): “And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind: and it was so.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A24&version=KJV | Genesis 1:27 (King James Version, public domain): “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A27&version=KJV | Genesis 2:5 (King James Version, public domain): “And every plant of the field before it was in the earth, and every herb of the field before it grew: for the LORD God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was not a man to till the ground.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A5&version=KJV | Genesis 2:7 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A7&version=KJV | Genesis 2:9 (King James Version, public domain): “And out of the ground made the LORD God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A9&version=KJV | Genesis 2:19 (King James Version, public domain): “And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A19&version=KJV | Genesis 2:22 (King James Version, public domain): “And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A22&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: two accounts side by side suggest the ancients kept the story for its meaning, not as minutes.

licoes.t: A single first couple? What genetics says
licoes.r: The text says Eve “was the mother of all living” (Gen 3:20). Population genetics measures the variety in our DNA and calculates how many people were needed to produce it: the ancestral population never fell below a few thousand individuals (estimates around 10,000) — source: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature10231. One couple cannot carry that much variation. Our DNA also holds pieces inherited from Neanderthals and Denisovans — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interbreeding_between_archaic_and_modern_humans.
licoes.a:
Correcting a common idea: 'Mitochondrial Eve' and 'Y-chromosome Adam' were not a couple. They lived at different times, tens of thousands of years apart depending on the study, and each lived among thousands of other people whose genes also reached us through other parts of the DNA — sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrial_Eve and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y-chromosomal_Adam.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 3:20 (King James Version, public domain): “And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A20&version=KJV | Genesis 1:28 (King James Version, public domain): “And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A28&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: we are one big family, but of thousands of grandparents, not two.

licoes.t: From dust and rib vs biology
licoes.r: The text: “the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground” (Gen 2:7) and “the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman” (Gen 2:22). What matches as an image: the body is made of common elements (carbon, oxygen, calcium). What doesn't: humans arose by gradual evolution; Homo sapiens is ≈300,000 years old (Jebel Irhoud fossils, Morocco) — source: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature22336 — and we share about 98–99% of comparable DNA with chimpanzees — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimpanzee_genome_project.
licoes.a:
Correcting a popular myth: men do NOT have one rib fewer. Men and women have 12 pairs — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib_cage. Even if a father lost a rib, it would not pass to his children: acquired traits are not inherited. Biologically there is no path to build an adult person from a bone.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 2:7 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A7&version=KJV | Genesis 2:21 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof;” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A21&version=KJV | Genesis 2:22 (King James Version, public domain): “And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A22&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: 'dust' can be read as humility: we came from the same matter as the rest of Earth.

licoes.t: The talking serpent, 'eating dust' and the tree of life
licoes.r: The serpent talks and argues (Gen 3:1) and is cursed: “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life” (Gen 3:14). Biology: snakes have no vocal cords or a brain capable of language — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake; all are carnivores, none eats dust; and fossils show snakes with little hind legs ≈95 million years ago (Najash), losing their legs gradually long before people existed — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Najash. The tree of life (Gen 2:9; 3:22) and the cherubim with a flaming sword (Gen 3:24) are supernatural claims: not verifiable.
licoes.a:
Context: a 'plant of life' stolen by a serpent also appears in the Epic of Gilgamesh, a Mesopotamian poem older than Genesis — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_of_Gilgamesh. Winged guardians at sacred entrances (lamassu) were common in the region's art — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamassu. These are cultural parallels, not proof of direct copying. Note: in Genesis the serpent is not called Satan; that identification came centuries later.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 3:1 (King James Version, public domain): “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A1&version=KJV | Genesis 3:14 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A14&version=KJV | Genesis 2:9 (King James Version, public domain): “And out of the ground made the LORD God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A9&version=KJV | Genesis 3:22 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A22&version=KJV | Genesis 3:24 (King James Version, public domain): “So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubim, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A24&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: talking animals are a mark of fable. The moral meaning may hold even without the zoology.

licoes.t: Death before sin? What fossils show
licoes.r: The traditional reading says death entered the world through sin: “by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin” (Romans 5:12), linked to Gen 2:17 and 3:19 (“dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return”). Fossils show billions of years of life and death before any human: stromatolites ≈3.5 billion years old, five mass extinctions (the dinosaurs' 66 million years ago) — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction_event — and even bone cancer in a ≈76-million-year-old dinosaur — source: https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(20)30171-6.
licoes.a:
More evidence: predators with hunting teeth, bones with bite marks, fossil prey inside predators, disease in ancient bones (paleopathology) — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleopathology. Death, disease and predation are far older than humanity. Some Christian readings take the 'death' of Genesis as spiritual, not physical; that's theology and does not change the fossils.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 2:17 (King James Version, public domain): “But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A17&version=KJV | Genesis 3:19 (King James Version, public domain): “In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A19&version=KJV | Romans 5:12 (King James Version, public domain): “Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans+5%3A12&version=KJV | Genesis 1:30 (King James Version, public domain): “And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A30&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: death has been part of life's cycle for billions of years. It is nature, not punishment.

licoes.t: Cain: his wife, the city and whom he feared
licoes.r: After killing Abel, Cain fears: “every one that findeth me shall slay me” (Gen 4:14). Who, if only Adam, Eve and he existed? He goes to the land of Nod (Gen 4:16) and “Cain knew his wife... and he builded a city” (Gen 4:17). The text doesn't say where the wife came from. A city needs many people; the first real cities, like Uruk, appear ≈6,000 years ago in societies of thousands — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruk. In the same line, Abel is a shepherd and Cain a farmer (Gen 4:2), and Tubal-cain already makes tools 'of brass and iron' (Gen 4:22): in real history, farming begins ≈11,500 years ago and large-scale iron ≈3,200 — sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neolithic_Revolution and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age.
licoes.a:
The traditional answer: Adam had 'sons and daughters' (Gen 5:4), and Cain would have married a sister. But that isn't in chapter 4, and it doesn't explain whom Cain feared or who populated a city. The simplest reading is that the story assumes, without saying, that other people existed — which fits genetics, not a single couple.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 4:2 (King James Version, public domain): “And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+4%3A2&version=KJV | Genesis 4:14 (King James Version, public domain): “Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth; and it shall come to pass, that every one that findeth me shall slay me.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+4%3A14&version=KJV | Genesis 4:16 (King James Version, public domain): “And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+4%3A16&version=KJV | Genesis 4:17 (King James Version, public domain): “And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+4%3A17&version=KJV | Genesis 4:22 (King James Version, public domain): “And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+4%3A22&version=KJV | Genesis 5:4 (King James Version, public domain): “And the days of Adam after he had begotten Seth were eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters:” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+5%3A4&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: a story written in an age of cities and iron projects its own world into the past.

licoes.r: Genesis 5 gives ages: “all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years” (Gen 5:5); Methuselah 969 (Gen 5:27). The longest documented human life is 122 years (Jeanne Calment, 1875–1997) — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Calment. Adding up the genealogies, Archbishop James Ussher (1650) dated creation to 4004 BC, about 6,000 years ago — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ussher_chronology. Archaeology shows more: Göbekli Tepe is ≈11,500 years old — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%B6bekli_Tepe; Jericho ≈11,000; the Chauvet cave paintings ≈36,000 — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauvet_Cave.
licoes.a:
Cultural context: huge ages for the ancients also appear in the Sumerian King List, where kings before the flood reign tens of thousands of years — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumerian_King_List. It was a way of saying 'the ancestors were great'. Comparing: Ussher gives ≈6,000 years; Homo sapiens ≈300,000 (50 times more); Earth 4.54 billion (750,000 times more).

Citations (check the text): Genesis 5:3 (King James Version, public domain): “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+5%3A3&version=KJV | Genesis 5:5 (King James Version, public domain): “And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+5%3A5&version=KJV | Genesis 5:27 (King James Version, public domain): “And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+5%3A27&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: huge numbers in ancient stories spoke of honour, not birth certificates.

licoes.t: Internal contradictions and the logic test
p: in the day you eat you will die
licoes.r:
Side by side, text only:
1) “in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die” (Gen 2:17) vs Adam lived 930 years (Gen 5:5). And the serpent said “Ye shall not surely die” (Gen 3:4).
2) God asks “Where art thou?” (Gen 3:9) vs belief in an all-knowing God.
3) “Behold, the man is become as one of us... lest he... eat, and live for ever” (Gen 3:22): God taking precautions against man, and speaking in the plural.
4) “Let us make man in our image” (Gen 1:26): plural in a monotheistic text.
5) Creation was “very good” (Gen 1:31), yet a “subtil” serpent was already there to deceive (Gen 3:1).
6) Different order of creation in Gen 1 and Gen 2 (lesson 4) and Cain's wife (lesson 9).
licoes.a:
Logic test of the God described in the text (only narrated acts, no diagnosis): Omniscience: if he knew they would eat, why put the tree within reach? If not, why ask 'where art thou'? Love: he punishes the couple, the serpent, the soil and (in the original-sin reading, Rom 5:12) all descendants. Justice: the couple did not yet know good and evil when they disobeyed, since that knowledge would come from the fruit; punishing someone for an act done before knowing wrong, and extending the penalty to children who took no part, clashes with the modern idea of personal justice. Theological answers exist (free will, 'spiritual death', majestic plural or heavenly council) and are cited with respect — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem_of_evil. The sum still shows tensions the text itself doesn't resolve.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 1:26 (King James Version, public domain): “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A26&version=KJV | Genesis 1:31 (King James Version, public domain): “And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A31&version=KJV | Genesis 2:17 (King James Version, public domain): “But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A17&version=KJV | Genesis 5:5 (King James Version, public domain): “And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+5%3A5&version=KJV | Genesis 3:1 (King James Version, public domain): “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A1&version=KJV | Genesis 3:9 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A9&version=KJV | Genesis 3:22 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A22&version=KJV | Romans 5:12 (King James Version, public domain): “Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans+5%3A12&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: asking is not offending. Mature faith can bear hard questions.

licoes.t: Where the story comes from: two sources and Mesopotamian myths
licoes.r: Scholars explain the repetitions in Genesis 1–2 as two joined sources: the Priestly (P) in Genesis 1 and the Yahwist (J) in Genesis 2–3 — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_hypothesis. And there are parallels with older Mesopotamian texts: in Enuma Elish the world arises from divided primordial waters and humanity is made to serve the gods (compare 'the deep' and 'the waters', Gen 1:2) — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/En%C3%BBma_Eli%C5%A1; in Atrahasis humans are shaped from clay mixed with divine blood (compare Gen 2:7) — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atra-Hasis; in the Adapa myth a man loses the chance to eat the food of eternal life — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adapa; and in Gilgamesh a serpent steals the plant that renewed youth (compare Gen 3:22) — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_of_Gilgamesh.
licoes.a:
Honest caution: these are parallels, not proof of copying. The Hebrew authors lived in the same cultural world and seem to have answered those stories with their own theology: one God, humans with the dignity of the 'image of God', no war among gods. That shows Genesis as human literature in dialogue with its time.

Citations (check the text): Genesis 1:2 (King James Version, public domain): “And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A2&version=KJV | Genesis 2:7 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+2%3A7&version=KJV | Genesis 3:22 (King James Version, public domain): “And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+3%3A22&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: every culture tells how it all began. Comparing them reveals what each people valued.

licoes.t: What is true and what is not (full table)
p: true or false adam and eve
licoes.r: Scientific sum of Adam and Eve: 26 claims checked, one per row, with verse and source. Result: ❌ 20 do not match reality, ✅ 4 match and ❔ 2 are not verifiable. What matches: humans came last, human childbirth is painful, the Tigris and Euphrates exist and humans have a moral conscience. What doesn't: the six days, the order of creation, the single couple, the dust and the rib, the talking serpent, death only after sin, 900-year lifespans and a 6,000-year-old world. Full table as cards, easy to read on a phone: open conteudo/tabela-adao-eva.html?lang=en or see below.
licoes.a:
Format: Claim (verse) · Verdict · Evidence — source.

1. The universe and Earth were made in six days (Genesis 2:2; 1:31)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Earth is about 4.54 billion years old (radiometric dating of meteorites and rocks); the universe about 13.8 billion. — https://pubs.usgs.gov/gip/geotime/age.html

2. There was light, day and night before the Sun existed (day 1 vs day 4) (Genesis 1:3; 1:16)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Day and night are Earth's rotation facing the Sun. The Sun (≈4.6 billion years) is older than Earth. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun

3. Fruit trees appeared before the Sun (day 3 vs day 4) (Genesis 1:11; 1:16)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Plants need sunlight; flowering and fruiting plants appear in fossils ≈130 million years ago, billions of years after the Sun. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowering_plant

4. Birds came before land animals (day 5 vs day 6) (Genesis 1:20; 1:24)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Land vertebrates exist since ≈370 million years ago; birds descend from theropod dinosaurs and appear ≈150 million years ago. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_of_birds

5. Great sea creatures (whales) came before land animals (Genesis 1:21)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Whales evolved from land mammals ≈50 million years ago (fossils such as Pakicetus and Ambulocetus). — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_cetaceans

6. Humans arrived last, after the other animals (Genesis 1:27)
   ✅ Matches reality
   Broadly true: Homo sapiens is ≈300,000 years old, long after most animal groups. — https://www.nature.com/articles/nature22336

7. Man was formed from the dust of the ground, already adult, in one act (Genesis 2:7)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   The human body is made of common natural elements (true as an image), but humans arose by gradual evolution, sharing DNA with other primates. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_evolution

8. Woman was made from a man's rib (Genesis 2:22; 2:21)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   There is no biological mechanism for this; men and women have the same number of ribs (12 pairs). — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib_cage

9. Adam named all the animals before woman was made (on the same day 6) (Genesis 2:20; 2:19)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   An estimated ≈8.7 million eukaryotic species exist; naming them all in a day is impossible. — https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371/journal.pbio.1001127

10. All humanity descends from a single couple (Genesis 3:20)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   The diversity of our DNA shows the ancestral population never fell below a few thousand people (estimates of ≈10,000). — https://www.nature.com/articles/nature10231

11. 'Mitochondrial Eve' and 'Y-chromosome Adam' prove the biblical couple (Genesis 3:20)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   They are ancestors of specific lineages, lived at different times (tens of thousands of years apart) and lived among thousands of other people. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrial_Eve

12. A serpent spoke and argued with the woman (Genesis 3:1; 3:4)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Snakes have no vocal cords, lips or a brain capable of language; they only hiss. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake

13. The serpent began crawling as a punishment (it had another form before) (Genesis 3:14)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Fossils show snakes with hind legs ≈95 million years ago (Najash); leg loss was gradual, long before humans. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Najash

14. Snakes eat dust (Genesis 3:14)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   All snakes are carnivores (rodents, eggs, fish, insects). They pick up scents with their tongue, which may have inspired the image. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake

15. There was no death before Adam's disobedience (Genesis 2:17; Romans 5:12)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Fossils record billions of years of life and death, five mass extinctions and even bone cancer in a ≈76-million-year-old dinosaur. — https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(20)30171-6

16. Human childbirth is painful (Genesis 3:16)
   ✅ Matches reality
   True: human birth is harder than in most primates. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obstetrical_dilemma

17. Childbirth pain is a punishment for Eve's disobedience (Genesis 3:16)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   The main scientific explanation is anatomical: a pelvis narrowed by walking on two legs and a large-headed baby (the 'obstetric dilemma', still debated in detail). Other mammals also feel pain giving birth. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obstetrical_dilemma

18. Eden was near the Tigris and Euphrates rivers (Genesis 2:14; 2:10)
   ✅ Matches reality
   Geographically true: these rivers exist in Mesopotamia, cradle of ancient cities. The Pishon and Gihon rivers were never securely identified. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_of_Eden

19. There was a tree whose fruit gave eternal life (Genesis 3:22; 2:9)
   ❔ Not verifiable
   It cannot be tested. No known plant stops ageing; the same idea (a plant of life) appears in the Epic of Gilgamesh. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_of_Gilgamesh

20. Cherubim and a flaming sword guard the way to Eden (Genesis 3:24)
   ❔ Not verifiable
   A supernatural claim, not verifiable. Winged guardian figures (such as the lamassu) were common in Mesopotamian art. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamassu

21. Cain, son of the first couple, found a wife and built a city (Genesis 4:17)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   A city requires a large population. The text does not say where the wife came from; the first cities (like Uruk) appear ≈6,000 years ago, in societies of thousands. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruk

22. Cain feared that 'whoever' found him would kill him (Genesis 4:14)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   By the story itself, only Adam, Eve and Cain would exist. The fear presupposes other people, which fits genetics, not a single couple. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wife_of_Cain

23. Farming, herding and iron tools arose within the first seven generations (Genesis 4:22; 4:2)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Farming began ≈11,500 years ago; large-scale iron working only ≈3,200 years ago. Thousands of years apart. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age

24. People lived 900 years or more (Adam 930, Methuselah 969) (Genesis 5:5; 5:27)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   The longest documented human lifespan is 122 years (Jeanne Calment). Ancient skeletons show no greater ages. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanne_Calment

25. Adding up the genealogies, the world would be ≈6,000 years old (Ussher: 4004 BC) (Genesis 5:3)
   ❌ Does not match reality
   Göbekli Tepe is ≈11,500 years old, Jericho ≈11,000, the Chauvet cave paintings ≈36,000 and Homo sapiens ≈300,000. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%B6bekli_Tepe

26. Humans have a moral conscience: they think about good and evil (Genesis 3:22; 3:5)
   ✅ Matches reality
   True as an observation: the ability to judge right and wrong is a human trait studied by psychology and neuroscience. The cause told (a fruit) is not verifiable. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morality#Neuroscience

Citations (check the text): Genesis 1:3 (King James Version, public domain): “And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A3&version=KJV | Genesis 1:11 (King James Version, public domain): “And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.” — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A11&version=KJV | Genesis 1:16 (King James Version, public domain): “And God made two great lights; licoes.t: Conhecimento Solar's opinion: honest verdict on Adam and Eve
licoes.r: Verdict: as literal history, Adam and Eve do not match reality. In the scientific sum, 20 of 26 claims don't match (six days, order of creation, single couple, rib, talking serpent, death only after sin, 930 years, a 6,000-year-old world), 4 match and 2 are not verifiable. The text itself carries two creation versions (Gen 1 and Gen 2) and gaps like Cain's wife (Gen 4:17). It is a human narrative, an origin myth in the technical sense: a story that explains who we are, with parallels in Mesopotamian myths. This is not mocking believers: many Jewish and Christian traditions read it symbolically. Origen, in the 3rd century, already found it absurd to imagine God planting a garden like a farmer; Augustine warned against using Genesis to contradict what is known about nature; and the Catholic Church accepts evolution (John Paul II, 1996).
licoes.a:
On repetition: an idea heard often since childhood feels true just because it is familiar; psychology calls this the illusory truth effect — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illusory_truth_effect. Those who believed were not foolish: they received the story from people they loved, who received it the same way. A calm invitation: read Genesis 1 to 5 yourself, check the verses and sources in this path, and decide freely. Sources for the symbolic reading: Origen, De Principiis IV — https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/04124.htm ; Augustine, De Genesi ad litteram — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Genesi_ad_litteram ; John Paul II, message on evolution (1996) — https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/messages/pont_messages/1996/documents/hf_jp-ii_mes_19961022_evoluzione.html

licoes.c: To contemplate: a story's value doesn't depend on it having happened. The question that remains: what does it want to teach me, and what do I choose to think for myself?

licoes.t: Who created the God of the Bible? The question and the method
licoes.r: This theme's question: does the God described in the Bible look more like a loving divine being, or like the mindset of the people who wrote about him, in a specific time and place? The same book says “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;” (Exodus 20:5) and also “He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.” (1 John 4:8). To understand this tension we follow what historical research, archaeology and psychology show, step by step, with the verse and the source for each claim.
licoes.a:
Two honest corrections first. One: the Bible was not written by a single person. Scholarship points to many authors, editors and schools over roughly a thousand years. Two: controlling people was one function of these texts, but not the only one. They also gave a small people an identity, explained wars and disasters, and held the group together in exile. Science neither proves nor disproves God's existence. What it can examine is the text: who wrote it, when and why.

Verses cited (check the text) (King James Version, public domain): Exodus 20:5 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Exodus+20%3A5&version=KJV | 1 John 4:8 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1+John+4%3A8&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: asking where an idea came from is not attacking those who love it. It is taking it seriously.

licoes.t: Who wrote the Bible: many hands, many centuries
licoes.r: Tradition says Moses wrote the first five books, but the text itself narrates his death (Deut 34). Since the 19th century, scholars have identified distinct sources with their own style, names for God and interests. The classic labels are J (Yahwist), E (Elohist), D (Deuteronomist) and P (Priestly), in the documentary hypothesis popularized by Richard Friedman's 'Who Wrote the Bible?' (1987). Many today prefer supplementary models, where a base text receives layers over time. A landmark is “And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the LORD. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.” (2 Kings 22:8): King Josiah (c. 622 BC) 'finds' a law book, which most scholars link to the core of Deuteronomy, written or revised to support his religious and political reform.
licoes.a:
The P layer and much of the final editing come from the Babylonian exile and after (6th–5th centuries BC). Genesis 1 is a priestly text, and even there a plural appears: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” (Genesis 1:26). So the God of the Bible was described by priests, court scribes, prophets and editors, each with concerns of their own: the temple, the king, loyalty to the one God, the survival of the people. Sources: documentary hypothesis — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_hypothesis ; Friedman — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who_Wrote_the_Bible%3F

Verses cited (check the text) (King James Version, public domain): 2 Kings 22:8 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2+Kings+22%3A8&version=KJV | Genesis 1:26 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Genesis+1%3A26&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: if many people wrote it, each left some of their fear, hope and politics in the text.

licoes.t: Where Yahweh came from: a storm god from the south
licoes.r: The name of God most used in the Hebrew Bible is YHWH (Yahweh). The oldest texts say he came from the south, from Seir, Edom and Teman, not from Israel: “And he said, The LORD came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them; he shined forth from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of saints: from his right hand went a fiery law for them.” (Deuteronomy 33:2) And also “LORD, when thou wentest out of Seir, when thou marchedst out of the field of Edom, the earth trembled, and the heavens dropped, the clouds also dropped water.” (Judges 5:4) Egyptian inscriptions from the 14th–13th centuries BC mention 'the Shasu of YHW', nomads of that region. So many scholars, like Thomas Römer in 'The Invention of God' (Harvard, 2015), think Yahweh began as a storm and war god of southern groups (Midianites or Kenites) and was only later adopted in Israel.
licoes.a:
A telling detail: a storm and war god is described with thunder, fire, earthquake and victory in battle, exactly the imagery of many ancient texts about Yahweh (Judg 5:4–5; Ps 18; Hab 3:3). It is a well-grounded hypothesis, not a closed fact, and details are still debated. Sources: Yahweh — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahweh ; Kenite hypothesis — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenite_hypothesis ; Römer — https://www.hup.harvard.edu/books/9780674504974

Verses cited (check the text) (King James Version, public domain): Deuteronomy 33:2 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy+33%3A2&version=KJV | Judges 5:4 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Judges+5%3A4&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: a god born as a tribe's warrior carries that tribe's way of thinking.

licoes.t: El, Asherah and 'God's wife': the Canaanite pantheon
licoes.r: In the Ugaritic texts (c. 1300 BC, in today's Syria), the high god is El, his consort is Asherah, and they have 70 sons, the 'sons of El', each linked to a people. The Bible keeps echoes of this. The KJV has “When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.” (Deuteronomy 32:8), but the Dead Sea Scrolls and the Septuagint read 'according to the number of the sons of God', which recalls El's 70 sons, one per nation. And the Psalm says: “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” (Psalms 82:1)
licoes.a:
Archaeology confirms a goddess worshipped alongside Yahweh. At Kuntillet Ajrud (c. 800 BC), jars carry the blessing 'by Yahweh of Samaria and his Asherah'. The Bible shows people baking cakes for the 'queen of heaven': “The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto other gods, that they may provoke me to anger.” (Jeremiah 7:18) And in Josiah's reform, “And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the door, to bring forth out of the temple of the LORD all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven: and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto Bethel.” (2 Kings 23:4) For centuries, many Israelites worshipped Yahweh along with other deities, and 'Yahweh alone' won later. Mark S. Smith, in 'The Early History of God', shows Yahweh absorbing El's titles and gradually the other gods' roles. Sources: Kuntillet Ajrud — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuntillet_Ajrud ; Asherah — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asherah ; Smith — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Early_History_of_God

Verses cited (check the text) (King James Version, public domain): Deuteronomy 32:8 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy+32%3A8&version=KJV | Psalms 82:1 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Psalms+82%3A1&version=KJV | Jeremiah 7:18 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Jeremiah+7%3A18&version=KJV | 2 Kings 23:4 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2+Kings+23%3A4&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: ideas about God changed over time. A changing image follows whoever draws it.

licoes.t: From many gods to one: monotheism is born in exile
licoes.r: The oldest texts don't deny that other gods exist. They demand that Israel serve Yahweh alone. That is monolatry: “For thou shalt worship no other god: for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God:” (Exodus 34:14) The Bible names neighboring gods plainly: “Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in mine eyes, and to keep my statutes and my judgments, as did David his father.” (1 Kings 11:33) Full monotheism, the idea that only one God exists, emerges strongly in Second Isaiah, written during the Babylonian exile (c. 540 BC): “I am the LORD, and there is none else, there is no God beside me: I girded thee, though thou hast not known me:” (Isaiah 45:5)
licoes.a:
Why in exile? Jerusalem and the temple were destroyed in 586 BC. A defeated people had two options: accept that Babylon's gods were stronger, or say Yahweh himself had used Babylon to punish Israel. The scribes chose the second. So Yahweh became responsible for everything, even evil: “I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the LORD do all these things.” (Isaiah 45:7) This is the root of 'punishment for sins': defeat becomes the people's guilt rather than God's weakness. Sources: monolatry — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monolatry ; exile — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babylonian_captivity

Verses cited (check the text) (King James Version, public domain): Exodus 34:14 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Exodus+34%3A14&version=KJV | Isaiah 45:5 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah+45%3A5&version=KJV | Isaiah 45:7 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah+45%3A7&version=KJV | 1 Kings 11:33 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1+Kings+11%3A33&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: when a people suffers it looks for an explanation. Guilt tends to be the one that binds most.

licoes.t: The warrior God and the kings of the ancient Near East
licoes.r: How Yahweh acts in war was the standard of the age. On the Mesha Stele (c. 840 BC, Louvre), the king of Moab says his god Chemosh ordered him to attack Nebo, and that he killed its 7,000 inhabitants, men, women and girls, because he had 'devoted them to destruction' (the same idea as the biblical 'herem'). The Bible itself tells of the war against this king and says that when he sacrificed his son, “Then he took his eldest son that should have reigned in his stead, and offered him for a burnt offering upon the wall. And there was great indignation against Israel: and they departed from him, and returned to their own land.” (2 Kings 3:27)
licoes.a:
Deuteronomy also copies the form of Assyrian vassal treaties. Esarhaddon's succession treaty (672 BC) required reporting even one's own relative who conspired against the king, and lists curses such as eating the flesh of one's own children. Compare “If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;” (Deuteronomy 13:6) and “And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the LORD thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee:” (Deuteronomy 28:53) Many scholars (Levinson, Steymans, Römer) see Judahite scribes swapping the Assyrian emperor for Yahweh as the 'great king' owed total loyalty. Sources: Mesha Stele — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesha_Stele ; herem — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herem_(war_or_property) ; Esarhaddon — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esarhaddon

Verses cited (check the text) (King James Version, public domain): 2 Kings 3:27 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=2+Kings+3%3A27&version=KJV | Deuteronomy 13:6 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy+13%3A6&version=KJV | Deuteronomy 28:53 — https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy+28%3A53&version=KJV
licoes.c: To contemplate: if the God of the text acts like the kings of the age, it is fair to ask who modeled whom.

licoes.r:
Here are the texts as they are, in full. Next to each, how the same order would be judged today under the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (1998).

1) Numbers 31, after the war against Midian, Moses says: “Now therefore kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman that hath known man by lying with him.” (Numbers 31:17) “But all the women children, that have not known a man by lying with him, keep alive for yourselves.” (Numbers 31:18) Today: genocide (art. 6), killing prisoners and children (art. 8) and sexual slavery (arts. 7.1.g and 8.2.b.xxii).

2) “But of the cities of these people, which the LORD thy God doth give thee for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth:” (Deuteronomy 20:16) “But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the LORD thy God hath commanded thee:” (Deuteronomy 20:17) Today: genocide (art. 6) and an order of 'no survivors', a war crime (art. 8.2.b.xii).

3) “Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.” (1 Samuel 15:3) Today: genocide (art. 6) and intentional attack on civilians (art. 8.2.b.i).

4) At Jericho: “And they utterly destroyed all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox, and sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword.” (Joshua 6:21) Today: genocide and a crime against humanity (arts. 6 and 7).

5) “And it came to pass, that at midnight the LORD smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.” (Exodus 12:29) Today: collective punishment of children for a ruler's decision, banned by Geneva Convention IV (art. 33).

6) The flood: “And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping things, and the fowl of the heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.” (Genesis 7:23) Today: extermination (art. 7.1.b).
licoes.a:
Behaviour traits these texts describe, without diagnosis: collective punishment (the innocent pay for the group), dehumanization of the other people (all become 'enemies' to destroy) and sparing only virgins treated as spoils. Diagnosing a literary character is neither possible nor honest. What can be said is: a human giving these orders today would stand trial for war crimes.

Two balancing facts: (1) archaeology indicates many of these conquests did not happen as told. Jericho, for example, was practically uninhabited at the time attributed to Joshua (Kathleen Kenyon, 1950s; Finkelstein, 'The Bible Unearthed'). These are identity narratives written centuries later, not war reports. (2) The pattern matches the Mesha Stele: this is how peoples of that age imagined a victorious god. Sources: Rome Statute — https://www.icc-cpi.int/sites/default/files/RS-Eng.pdf ; Geneva IV art. 33 — https://ihl-databases.icrc.org/en/ihl-treaties/gciv-1949/article-33 ; Jericho — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jericho

licoes.c: To contemplate: if an order would be a crime coming from a man, why would it be goodness coming from a text? Ask calmly and answer for yourself.

licoes.t: The hardest verses (2): collective punishment and control by fear
licoes.r:
1) Against anyone, even family, who calls to another god: “If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;” (Deuteronomy 13:6) “But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.” (Deuteronomy 13:9) “And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.” (Deuteronomy 13:10) Today: execution for belief, which violates the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (arts. 6 and 18).

2) In a vision, God sends six men through Jerusalem: “And to the others he said in mine hearing, Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity:” (Ezekiel 9:5) “Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women: but come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house.” (Ezekiel 9:6) Today: mass murder of civilians, a crime against humanity (art. 7.1.a).

3) Threat of extreme famine: “And ye shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters shall ye eat.” (Leviticus 26:29) Today, starving civilians as a weapon is a war crime (art. 8.2.b.xxv).

4) Elisha curses the boys in the name of the Lord: “And he went up from thence unto Bethel: and as he was going up by the way, there came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said unto him, Go up, thou bald head; go up, thou bald head.” (2 Kings 2:23) “And he turned back, and looked on them, and cursed them in the name of the LORD. And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them.” (2 Kings 2:24) Today: disproportionate killing of minors over a verbal insult.

5) Against Samaria: “Samaria shall become desolate; for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword: their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up.” (Hosea 13:16) Today: a war crime against children and pregnant women (art. 8).

6) After the golden calf: “And he said unto them, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.” (Exodus 32:27) “And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.” (Exodus 32:28) Today: collective execution on religious grounds.

7) A man gathering sticks on the sabbath: “And the LORD said unto Moses, The man shall be surely put to death: all the congregation shall stone him with stones without the camp.” (Numbers 15:35) “And all the congregation brought him without the camp, and stoned him with stones, and he died; as the LORD commanded Moses.” (Numbers 15:36) Today: death penalty for working on a holy day, against the right to life (ICCPR art. 6).
licoes.a:
Behaviour traits described, without diagnosis: demand for exclusive loyalty (the 'jealous' one of Ex 34:14), surveillance and denunciation inside the family, collective punishment, threat as a means of obedience and disproportionate punishment. In the psychology of relationships this cluster (isolate, watch, threaten, punish whoever leaves) has a name: coercive control, described by sociologist Evan Stark (2007). It is not a diagnosis of God. It describes the kind of relationship these texts build between the people and authority, the same one Assyrian treaties built between vassal and emperor. Sources: Rome Statute — https://www.icc-cpi.int/sites/default/files/RS-Eng.pdf ; ICCPR — https://www.ohchr.org/en/instruments-mechanisms/instruments/international-covenant-civil-and-political-rights ; coercive control — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coercive_control
