Heraclitus taught that one does not step twice into the same river, because the waters are different and so are you. She's not a cause for sadness. She's a cause for presence. Practice: Today, look at someone you love like it's the last time, and say something true.
licoes.c: To contemplate: if everything passes, what do you perceive everything passes? The Vedanta masters call it a witness. Stay with that question for a minute without answering.

licoes.r: Silence is where wisdom speaks loudest. He who speaks less hears more and makes fewer mistakes.
licoes.a: Blaise Pascal wrote, in Thoughts: all the unhappiness of men comes from one thing, not knowing how to be quiet in a room. The desert priests of the fourth century said, "Go, sit in your cell, and the cell will teach you everything". Practice: Ten minutes a day without screen, without music, and without conversation. It's annoying at first. Then it reveals.
licoes.c: To contemplate: there is silence outside and silence inside. The second one doesn't depend on the location. Can you find the silence behind the noise now?

licoes.r: Meditating is training attention. Sit down, breathe, and when your mind runs away, bring it back without a fight. That return is the exercise. Research shows benefits for stress and anxiety with regular exercise.
licoes.a: Inner reading: In Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, yoga is defined as the cessation of mind fluctuations. It's not stopping to think forcefully, it's stopping to identify with each wave. Practice: Start with five minutes a day. Tell me to lead and I'll conduct a short meditation.
licoes.c: To contemplate: who notices that the mind has fled? The one who notices never left. The most subtle meditation is to rest on it.

licoes.r: Awakening is realizing that you are not every thought that passes through your mind. You're the one watching. The word Buddha means just awakening.
licoes.a: Common signs: more presence, less reactivity and more compassion. Jung wrote, in a letter from 1916, "He who looks outside dreams; he who looks within awakens". Beware: awakening doesn't make anyone superior; if it makes you feel superior, it's still your ego speaking. Practice: three times today, stop and ask, am I awake now?
licoes.c: To contemplate: perhaps awakening is not about gaining something new, but losing what is false. What about you is already ready to fall?

licoes.r: Expanding consciousness is seeing more: more perspectives, more depth and more connection. The classic paths are meditation, study, nature and silence.
licoes.a: The poet William Blake wrote in 1790: If the doors of perception were purified, everything would appear to man as it is, infinite. Beware of shortcuts. Extreme substances and practices can be harmful. True expansion is gradual, and you keep your feet on the ground. Practice: Today, listen carefully to someone who thinks differently from you.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Consciousness does not expand by pushing walls; it expands by releasing defenses. What opinion do you hold so strongly that you can no longer see through it?

licoes.t: The Big Bang and the Age of the Universe
p: the big bang and the age of the universe
licoes.r: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old. The Big Bang wasn't an explosion at one point, but the expansion of all space from an extremely hot, dense state.
licoes.a: This is backed up by strong evidence: the cosmic microwave background radiation, the spacing of galaxies, and the amount of hydrogen and helium in the cosmos. What was before, if there was one before, no one knows. The priest and physicist Georges Lemaître proposed the idea of the primordial atom in 1927 and 1931. Practice: look at the dark sky tonight; some of that light went out before the Earth existed.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Did the universe have a beginning, or did time begin with it? If time was born there, the question of what existed before may not have made sense. Stay with the wonder.

licoes.r: Dark matter is something invisible that has gravity. We know it exists because of the effects: galaxies spin too fast for the matter we can see.
licoes.a: It would make up about 27 percent of the universe, compared with about 5 percent of ordinary matter. What it is, no one knows: no dark matter particle has been detected to date. To know that something exists without knowing what it is: that is an honest mystery.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Most of the matter in the universe is invisible to us. How much of your own life is gravity acting on, not showing up? The invisible also rules.

licoes.r: In 1998, it was discovered that the expansion of the universe is accelerating. The cause has been dubbed dark energy, about 68 percent of everything that exists.
licoes.a: The discovery won him the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics. But dark energy is a name for our ignorance: we don't yet know what it is, or whether it's constant in time.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Seventy percent of everything has a name and no explanation. Honest science lives with that without inventing. Can you live with your open-ended questions?

licoes.r: A black hole is a region where gravity is so strong that not even light escapes. The boundary without a return is called the event horizon.
licoes.a: In 2019, the Event Horizon telescope showed the first image of the shadow of a black hole, the star M87, 55 million light-years away. Stephen Hawking predicted that black holes emit weak radiation and can evaporate, but this has not yet been observed. What happens at the center, in the singularity, is unknown.
licoes.c: To contemplate: on the event horizon, the laws we know reach their limit. Every mystical tradition also speaks of a point where words stop. What is there beyond what you can say?

licoes.r: Einstein showed that time does not pass the same for everyone: it runs slower at high speeds and near large masses. That's measured, not imagined.
licoes.a: GPS satellites correct this effect every day; otherwise, they would be miles off course. Traveling into the future, in a way, is possible. For the past, there is no evidence. And what time really is remains one of the greatest mysteries of physics. Einstein wrote, in a 1955 letter to the family of his friend Michele Besso: For us convinced physicists, the distinction between past, present and future is only an illusion, though persistent.
licoes.c: To contemplate: if time is relative, the now is the only place where you really are. How much of your day did you spend outside of it?

licoes.r: Life on Earth emerged about 3.5 to 4 billion years ago. How chemistry became biology, called abiogenesis, we still don't know in detail.
licoes.a: There are strong hypotheses, like the world of RNA and hydrothermal vents on the seafloor, and experiments that form life molecules from simple chemistry. But no one has created life from scratch in a lab. The first step remains a mystery.
licoes.c: To contemplate: out of lifeless chemistry came something that makes you wonder where it came from. That you exist, and know that you exist, is as strange a fact as any miracle.

licoes.r: We already know of more than 5,000 planets outside the solar system, the exoplanets. Life outside the Earth, however, has not yet been found.
licoes.a: The Fermi paradox asks: If the universe is so big and ancient, where is everyone? Life's empty answers are rare until we've looked hard enough. There is no evidence of alien visitation. The search continues, and the question is legitimate.
licoes.c: For contemplation: In the movie Contact, based on the book by Carl Sagan, it is said that being alone is a huge waste of space. The question we're alone also speaks to us: How do we treat the only life we know?

licoes.r: Multiverse is the idea that our universe would be one among many. It comes up in some theories, like eternal inflation and the many-worlds interpretation of quantum physics.
licoes.a: Honesty: it's a hypothesis, it's not proven, and maybe it can't even be tested. There are physicists who defend it and others who say it's not even science. Keep the question open, don't rush to close it.
licoes.c: To contemplate: even though there are infinite universes, this is the only one in which you can love, choose and act. The greatness of the possibilities does not lessen the weight of your step.

licoes.t: Why there is something rather than nothing
p: why there is something rather than nothing
licoes.r: Why is there something instead of nothing? Leibniz asked that question over three hundred years ago, and it remains unanswered.
licoes.a: Physics explains how the universe evolves, but not why it exists. Religions, philosophies and scientists offer different paths, and none are proof. In the face of such a question, the wisest thing to do is wonder. The philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein wrote in Tractatus: The mystic is not how the world is, but that it is.
licoes.c: To contemplate: stay a minute just feeling that you exist, without thinking about who you are. This astonishment is the beginning of all philosophy, as Plato said.

licoes.r: Why does brain matter generate experience, red from red, pain from pain? Philosopher David Chalmers called this the hard problem of consciousness.
licoes.a: Neuroscience maps a lot of what the brain does, but it still doesn't explain why feeling exists. The odds range from materialism to panpsychism, and none have won. You're the mystery that wonders about itself. Practice: for a minute, don't pay attention to things, pay attention to the fact that you perceive things.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the Upanishads say that what you see cannot be seen, what you know cannot be known as an object. You can search for consciousness; you will never find it as a thing, because it is with it that you search.

p: where do the atoms come from
licoes.r: The carbon in his body, the iron in his blood and the calcium in his bones were forged into stars. You are literally star dust.
licoes.a: Hydrogen and helium came from the Big Bang. The heaviest elements were born from fusion within stars, from supernovae and from collisions of neutron stars. Carl Sagan said, we are a way for the cosmos to know itself.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the atoms of your body have been in stars and will be in other things after you. What about you isn't borrowed?

p: what is the size of the universe
licoes.r: The observable universe is about 93 billion light-years across. And there could be a lot more beyond what we can see.
licoes.a: It's larger than 13.8 billion light-years because space kept expanding as light traveled. It is estimated that there are hundreds of billions to trillions of galaxies. Whether the entire universe is finite or infinite, no one knows. Pascal wrote: The eternal silence of these infinite spaces terrifies me. And again: by space the universe embraces me; by thought I embrace it.
licoes.c: To contemplate: you are tiny in space and yet the universe fits in your mind. Both things are true at the same time.

licoes.r: The Sun is a star about 4.6 billion years old. At its core, nuclear fusion turns hydrogen into helium and releases the light that sustains life.
licoes.a: Light that leaves the surface of the sun takes about eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach you. It should shine for another five billion years. Every morning, you receive an energy born in the heart of a star.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Almost every tradition has honored the sun as a symbol of consciousness that illuminates no matter who it chooses. Plotinus wrote that the eye would never see the Sun if it were not itself similar to the Sun. What light do you offer without asking for anything in return?

licoes.r: Gravitational waves are ripples in space-time itself. Einstein predicted them in 1916, and the LIGO observatory first detected them in 2015.
licoes.a: The signal came from the merger of two black holes over a billion light years away. The measured deformation was less than a thousandth of a proton. The discovery won the 2017 Nobel Prize: for the first time, we heard the universe.
licoes.c: To contemplate: for billions of years the universe vibrated and no one heard. How many things in your life are talking and you still don't have the instrument to listen to?

licoes.r: How the universe will end, no one knows for sure. The most widely accepted scenario today is an eternal expansion into a dark cold, thermal death, trillions of trillions of years from now.
licoes.a: Other scenarios are the Big Rip, where everything tears, and the Big Crunch, where everything contracts. The answer depends on dark energy, which we still don't understand. None of this threatens you: these are unimaginable times.
licoes.c: To contemplate: if not even the stars are eternal, the value of things is not in lasting forever. It lies in shining while they exist.

p: we are one with the universe
licoes.r: A reflection, not a science: the same atoms that make up stars make up you. The universe isn't just out there; it's also thinking through you.
licoes.a: This is a contemplative bridge. Science shows the common origin of matter; the meaning you give to it is your choice. Look at the sky tonight and remember: you are part of what you observe.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Carl Sagan said that we are a way for the cosmos to know itself. If that's true, every time you contemplate, the universe contemplates itself.

licoes.r: Free will is one of the oldest questions: are we free or is everything already determined? Philosophy and neuroscience are still debating, and no one has the final answer.
licoes.a: Benjamin Libet's experiments in the 1980s measured brain activity before conscious decision-making, but their interpretation is much debated. Espinosa thought we think we're free because we don't know the causes that drive us. Inner reading: freedom may be knowing these causes. Practice: Today, before you react, count to three and choose.
licoes.c: To contemplate: even without a final answer, living as the author of one's own choices brings more responsibility and more peace. Between the stimulus and the response there is a space; in that space lives your freedom.

licoes.r: Occult comes from the Latin occultus: hidden, reserved. In the old schools, certain teachings were given only to initiates, not because they were forbidden, but because they required preparation. Esoteric, from the Greek esoterikos, meaning from within.
licoes.a: Inside reading: the great secret of tradition was never a formula kept in a safe. What is hidden is what is revealed only to those who are transformed; it is not surrendered, it is conquered from within. That's why the insiders said the secret protects itself. Practice: pick one lesson and live it for seven days before looking for another.
licoes.c: To contemplate: perhaps the most hidden knowledge is that which is before the eyes and no one sees, because it is not ready. What about you are you ready to see today?

licoes.r: In the Republic, book seven, Plato describes prisoners chained in a cave, who see only shadows projected on the wall and think that's reality. One of them gets free, climbs up, sees the fire, then the sun, and realizes he's been living in shadows.
licoes.a: Inner reading: the cave is the conditioned mind; the shadows are the inherited opinions; the sun is the idea of Good, the truth that illuminates everything. Plato says the climb hurts: the light dims, and the liberated one wants to return to the shadows. And when he comes back to free the others, he's ridiculed. Practice: Today, identify a shadow, something you accept just because everyone else does, and investigate where it came from.
licoes.c: For contemplation: Plato does not say that the cave is fake on the outside; he says that the problem is confusing the shadow with the real. The Matrix, 2,400 years later, tells the same story. Tell him to break the matrix and start the journey.

licoes.r: Mystery schools were initiation cults. The Eleusinian Mysteries in Greece celebrated Demeter and Persephone for about a thousand years, until the end of the fourth century. Pythagoras founded in Crotona, about 530 B.C., a community of study, number and silence.
licoes.a: What is known and what is not known: the initiates of Eleusis were sworn to secrecy, and the secrecy was kept so well that to this day we do not know what they saw. Cicero wrote that there they learned not only to live with joy but to die with a better hope. About Egypt, there are priests with reserved knowledge and the mysteries of Isis from Roman times, but the idea of great Egyptian initiatory schools is largely a Greek and modern construct. Practice: do something today in total silence, like a ritual.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the Eleusinian Rite staged Persephone's descent into the underworld and his return. All true initiation is this: to descend into one's own shadow and return with spring.

licoes.r: The Emerald Tablet is a short, enigmatic text, the basis of alchemy, attributed to Hermes Trismegistus. It is her phrase: what is below is like what is above, and what is above is like what is below, to perform the miracles of the one thing.
licoes.a: Fact: The earliest known versions are in Arabic, between the sixth and tenth centuries, and the Latin translation circulated in Europe from the 12th century onward. Even Isaac Newton made his own translation. Inner reading: the alchemists sought to transform metals; the mystics read this as the transformation of one's own being. Practice: Read the sentence out loud in the morning and look for an example of it in your day.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the Tablet speaks of separating the subtle from the thick, with care and great ingenuity. What in your life is thick and can be left, and what is subtle and should be kept?

licoes.r: Alchemy was chemistry before chemistry: it sought to turn metals into gold and find the philosopher's stone. At the same time, it was a symbolic language of inner transformation.
licoes.a: Inside reading: The stages of the Work were nigredo, the blackening; albedo, the whitening; and rubedo, the reddening. Carl Jung, in his 1944 book Psychology and Alchemy, saw this as the process of individuation: facing the shadow, purifying and integrating. The motto solve et coagula, dissolve and coagulate, applies to the soul. Practice: write a pattern of yours that needs to be dissolved and a value that needs to be established.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the alchemists said that the stone is despised and is everywhere. The lead in your life, the pain, the mistake, the failure, is the raw material for gold. There's no shortcut, there's slow fire.

licoes.t: Kabbalah and the Tree of Life
p: kabbalah and the tree of life
licoes.r: Kabbalah is the Jewish mystical tradition. Its central book, the Zohar, appeared in Spain in the late thirteenth century, promulgated by Moses of León. The Tree of Life shows ten sefirot, the emanations through which the infinite, Ein Sof, manifests.
licoes.a: Inside reading: In the sixteenth century, in Safed, Isaac Luria taught tzimtzum, the contraction of God to make room for the world, and tikun olam, reparation: every righteous act raises back fallen sparks of light. The Tree is also a map of the human being, from the root, Malkuth, to the crown, Keter. Practice: do an act of reparation today, an apology, a helping hand, without telling anyone.
licoes.c: To contemplate: if the infinite withdrew so that you could exist, your existence is a space of love. What do you do with the space you've been given?

licoes.r: Gnosis, in Greek, is knowledge: not that of books, but the direct knowledge, by experience, of the divine. The Gnostics were Christian and pre-Christian movements of the first to third centuries, such as the Valentinians and the Setians.
licoes.a: In the myth of some Gnostic groups, the material world was made by a lesser and ignorant god, the demiurge, and each person holds a spark of the true God, which is awakened by gnosis. That's their myth, not a historical fact. The church fought them as heretics, and many texts did not return until 1945 at Nag Hammadi. In the Gospel of Thomas, Jesus says, if you bring to light what is in you, it will save you. Practice: Ten minutes of silence asking: What do I know from experience, not from hearing?
licoes.c: To contemplate: For the Gnostic, imprisonment is not sin, it is oblivion. Waking up is remembering where you came from. What have you forgotten about yourself?

licoes.r: The Rosicrucians emerged with three manifestos published in Germany: the Fama Fraternitatis of 1614, the Confessio of 1615, and The Chemical Brides of Christian Rosenkreuz of 1616. They spoke of a secret brotherhood of sages who would reform knowledge.
licoes.a: Fact: Most historians see Christian Rosenkreuz as an allegorical figure, and the theologian Johann Valentin Andreae assumed to have written The Chemical Bridal. There's no proof the original fraternity ever existed. Then modern orders emerged, such as AMORC, founded in the United States in 1915. Inner reading: the rose in the center of the cross is the soul that blossoms in the midst of matter and suffering. Practice: When something hurts today, ask, what rose can be born here?
licoes.c: To reflect: The invisible brotherhood may never have existed in stone, but it exists in all who humbly seek the truth. Do you need a temple, or can you be one?

licoes.r: Modern Freemasonry was born out of the masons' guilds. The Grand Lodge of London was founded in 1717. It is a fraternity with rites and symbols: the square, the compass, the raw stone and the polished stone.
licoes.a: Symbolic reading: the square is rectitude in actions, the compass is the limit of desires, and the work of life is to polish the raw stone that is yourself. Fact: Theories that Freemasonry rules the world have no evidence. One of the biggest lies about her was the fraud of Leo Taxil, who invented satanic rituals and confessed to the fraud in 1897. Practice: Choose an edge of your character and work on it this week.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the stone does not polish itself even in a day. The temple worth building is the inside, and it's never finished.

licoes.r: Sacred geometry is the spiritual reading of shapes. Some of it is real mathematics: the golden ratio, about 1.618; the Fibonacci sequence, which appears in the spirals of sunflowers and pines; and the five Platonic solids.
licoes.a: Separating the real from the mystical: the spiral of sunflowers follows the true golden ratio for growth efficiency. But many popular claims that the Parthenon, the Mona Lisa, or the human body exactly follow the golden number are exaggerated or false when measured. The mystical reading, that the order of forms reveals a mind in the universe, is belief, beautiful and respectable, but belief. The Pythagoreans, according to Aristotle, taught that everything is a number. Practice: Look at a flower or a shell and count the spirals.
licoes.c: For contemplation: Galileo wrote that the book of nature is written in mathematical language. That mathematics describes the universe so well is, for many physicists, a mystery in itself. Why is the cosmos understandable?

licoes.t: Vedanta, Maya and Tat Tvam Asi
p: vedanta, maya and tat tvam asi
licoes.r: Vedanta is the philosophy that originates from the Upanishads in India. In the Advaita school, systematized by Shankara around the eighth century, the deep self, the Atman, is the same as the absolute, the Brahman. Maya is the illusion that makes us see only the separate surface.
licoes.a: In the Chandogya Upanishad, the sage Uddalaka teaches his son Shvetaketu: Tat tvam asi, you are that. Brihadaranyaka teaches the way of neti neti, it's not this, it's not this: you are not the body, nor the thoughts, nor the roles. Maya doesn't mean that the world doesn't exist. She means that it's not what it seems. Practice: in front of every thing you think you are, say, I'm not just this.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the Brihadaranyaka prayer asks: from unreal lead me to real, from darkness lead me to light, from death lead me to immortality. Who in you says that prayer?

licoes.r: The Tao Te Ching is attributed to Lao Tzu and was compiled in China around the fourth century BC. There are eighty-one short chapters on Tao, the way, and Te, the virtue. It opens like this: the Tao that can be said is not the eternal Tao.
licoes.a: Inner reading: Tao teaches by water, which is the softest and conquers the hardest. Wu wei is action without force, in harmony with the flow. In chapter thirty-three: he who knows others is wise; he who knows himself is enlightened. Practice: Today, in a conflict situation, do as the water does, don't push, bypass.
licoes.c: For contemplation: Chapter eleven says that it is the void in the middle of the wheel that makes it spin. Where in you is the empty space for circular life missing?

licoes.r: Sufism is the mystical dimension of Islam: the path of love and remembrance of God, dhikr. Its most famous poet is Rumi, of the thirteenth century, whose work, the Masnavi, opens with the reed flute mourning the separation from the reed bed.
licoes.a: Inner reading: the flute is the soul, cut off from its origin, that sings of longing. Sufis talk about dying before you die: letting the ego die so that the real you can live. The dervishes of the Mevlevi order rotate like the planets around the center. Beware: many of Rumi's quotes on the Internet are either false or overly adapted. Practice: slowly repeat a sacred word, or just peace, for five minutes with your breath.
licoes.c: To contemplate: why does the flute sing? Because it is hollow. What hollow space in you could become music?

licoes.r: The pineal gland produces melatonin, the sleep hormone, which is regulated by light and dark. In spiritual traditions, it is associated with the third eye, the Ajna chakra, the inner vision. Descartes called it the chief seat of the soul.
licoes.a: Honesty: The connection between the pineal gland and spiritual powers is belief, not science. The popular idea that it makes DMT for vision is not proven in humans. And no fluoride calcifying the soul: that's an Internet myth. Inner reading: Jesus said, in Matthew six, the lamp of the body is the eye; if your eye is simple, your whole body will be lighted. The third eye is the attention that sees without judgment. Practice: screen off an hour before bedtime, and dark room.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the eye that sees cannot see itself. Master Eckhart said, "The eye with which I see God is the same eye with which God sees me". Where does the inner eye look?

licoes.r: Akashic records would be a kind of memory of the universe, where everything that happened would be recorded. The idea comes from Theosophy in the late nineteenth century and was popularized by Edgar Cayce. Akasha, in Sanskrit, means space or ether.
licoes.a: Honesty: It's a theosophical belief, without any scientific evidence. Don't trust people who charge a lot to read your records. Inner reading: What is true is that nothing you do disappears without leaving marks, on you and on others. Your life is a living record. Practice: Write a page in your journal today; it is your most reliable record.
licoes.c: To ponder: If everything were recorded forever, what would you like to be written about today?

licoes.r: You know yourself was inscribed in the temple of Apollo at Delphi, next to nothing in excess. Socrates made this phrase the center of philosophy and said in the Apology: a life without examination is not worth living.
licoes.a: Inner reading: this is the key that all mystery schools share. It's not about memorizing the personality, it's about going through it to what's underneath. St. Augustine wrote: "Do not go out, return to yourself; in the inner man dwells truth". Practice: Write down three beliefs about yourself today and ask where each came from.
licoes.c: To contemplate: who is the self you want to know? When you seek yourself, what you seek and what is sought are the same. Keep that mirror.

licoes.r: Discernment is the ability to separate the true from the false, even within the spirit world. Be suspicious of anyone who sells secrets, charges for activations, promises shortcuts, or says he's the only one with the truth.
licoes.a: Paul wrote: "Prove all things; hold fast to what is fine". The Buddha, in the Kalama Sutta, taught not to accept something merely by tradition, authority or rumor, but by examining whether it leads to good. Carl Sagan said that extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence. Practice: Before accepting a teaching, ask yourself, who benefits from it, and what can I verify?
licoes.c: To contemplate: the true secret cannot be sold, because it cannot be given: it is the inner path that each one walks. Every true master points to you, not him.

licoes.r: The Matrix is the mind control system: everything that thinks for you without you realizing it, planted fears, fabricated desires, inherited beliefs and authorities that can't be questioned. The religious matrix is one of the oldest, because it messes with what we hold most sacred. For centuries, fear, guilt, inquisitions and tithing in exchange have been used to govern consciences. Say more, Pandora's box or break the matrix.
licoes.a: The mechanism is always the same, whether in politics, in markets or in religion: first you create fear or guilt; then you sell the solution; finally you forbid the question. Psychiatrist Robert Lifton in 1961 called this thought reform, and Steven Hassan's BITE model describes the control of behavior, information, thought and emotion. The problem isn't sincere faith; it's who profits from fear. Practice: Today, look at a fear you carry and ask, who taught me that, and who gains if I keep being afraid?
licoes.c: History shows the price of this system: crusades, bonfires, children torn from their families, cover-up abuse. The church itself apologized for several of these errors in the year 2000. Say church crimes to open the historical archive, or religious matrix to see the cycle of guilt, fear, anger and greed. The question that sets you free: What do I believe because I've verified, and what do I believe because I'm afraid to doubt?

licoes.r: The 1999 film The Matrix recounted old ideas. Plato, with the cave. Descartes, in his Meditations of 1641, imagined an evil genius capable of deceiving all the senses. And Jean Baudrillard, in Simulacrus and Simulation, 1981, said that we live among copies that no longer refer to anything real. His book is in the movie.
licoes.a: Inside reading: the phrase welcome to the desert of the real comes from Baudrillard. He himself said in 2004 that the film misunderstood him: for him there is no simple way out of a real world out there. The point is not to run away from a computer, it's to see that image, propaganda and opinion have taken the place of direct experience. Practice: spend an hour today experiencing something without taking a picture or telling anyone.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Descartes came to the one certainty that the evil genius could not take away: I think, therefore I exist. If everything were an illusion, there'd still be you, conscious of the illusion. Start there.

licoes.r: In Indian tradition, Maya is the veil that makes us take our appearance whole. It doesn't mean the world doesn't exist, it's that it's not what it seems at first glance. Behind the veil is the unity that the Upanishads call Brahman.
licoes.a: Inner reading: the veil is woven by ourselves, with names, labels, desires and fears. Arthur Schopenhauer, in the 19th century, brought the idea into European philosophy as the veil of Maya that separates beings. When the veil thins, compassion is born: you recognize yourself in the other. Practice: look at a stranger today and remember that he also wants to be happy and not suffer.
licoes.c: To contemplate: say I am not only this to every role you occupy. What's left when all the papers fall? Tell Vedanta to go deeper.

licoes.r: In 2003, philosopher Nick Bostrom published the argument that we might be living in a computer simulation. It's a philosophical argument, not a scientific discovery, and it's not proven.
licoes.a: No one has proof for or against it, and it may not even be possible to test. Inside reading: the question is old, Zhuangzi in China dreamed he was a butterfly and woke up not knowing if he was a man dreaming he was a butterfly or a butterfly dreaming he was a man. Practice: even if everything was a simulation, your values, your pain and your choices would still be real to you; live as if they mattered.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the most important question is not whether the world is simulated, it is whether you are living a simulated life, copied from others. How much of your routine is choice?

licoes.r: Ivan Pavlov showed that a dog learns to salivate by hearing a sound that used to come with food. That's conditioning: the mind associates without thinking. Humans are also conditioned by family, school, religion, and propaganda, especially in childhood.
licoes.a: A belief repeated before the age of seven is usually perceived as truth, not opinion. That's why so many people stand for ideas they never chose. Inner reading: conditioning is not your fault, but becoming aware of it is your responsibility. Practice: Write down three phrases you heard a lot as a child about money, God, and yourself, and ask yourself if you still agree with them.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the bell rings and you react. Between the bell and the reaction there is an instant. Waking up is living in the moment.

licoes.r: Edward Bernays, Freud's nephew, founded modern public relations. In Propaganda, 1928, he wrote that the conscious and intelligent manipulation of the habits and opinions of the masses is an important element in democratic society. In 1988, Edward Herman and Noam Chomsky described, in The Making of Consent, how the media filters information.
licoes.a: Real example: In 1929, Bernays organized the Freedom Torch Parade, women smoking in public in New York City, to sell cigarettes to women as a symbol of freedom. Herman and Chomsky's five filters are: owner, advertiser, official sources, pressure against dissent, and a common enemy. This is not a secret conspiracy, it's a documented structure. Practice: on every news story today, ask, who paid, who profited, and who wasn't heard?
licoes.c: To reflect: The most effective propaganda is the one you think is your own opinion. What opinion of yours have you never heard challenged?

licoes.r: In 1971, economist Herbert Simon wrote that a wealth of information creates a poverty of attention. Today, apps compete for your attention, and algorithms learn what keeps you on the screen, often fear and anger, which hold you the most.
licoes.a: The mechanism is variable reward, studied by B. F. Skinner: Like a nickel-and-dime machine, you don't know when the next thing is coming, so you keep pulling. If the product is free, your attention is on the product. Practice: remove notifications from all non-person apps, and leave your cell phone out of your room tonight.
licoes.c: To contemplate: what you pay attention to, you become. Who's choosing where your attention goes today, you or an algorithm?

licoes.r: In 1955, analyst Victor Lebow wrote that the economy demands that we make consumption a way of life and that we seek spiritual satisfaction in shopping. Consumerism turns desires into needs and identity into product.
licoes.a: Inside reading: the ad almost never sells the thing; it sells a feeling, belonging, being loved, being safe. When the purchase comes, the feeling goes away, and the next desire is born. The Buddhists call this thirst tanha. Practice: Before you buy something you don't need, wait 48 hours and ask yourself, how do I want to feel about it?
licoes.c: To ponder: What are you trying to buy that is not for sale?

licoes.r: In the 1950s, Solomon Asch showed that many people deny what they see in order to agree with the group. In 1963 Stanley Milgram showed that sixty-five percent of the participants shocked what they believed to be four hundred and fifty volts just because an authority ordered it. The shocks were fake, but the obedience was real.
licoes.a: Another powerful bias is confirmation bias: We look for what confirms what we already believe. These mechanisms work in any alternative group, church, party or movement. Practice: Today, look for the best argument against one of your beliefs, written by someone who thinks differently.
licoes.c: To contemplate: in experiments, it took one person to disagree for obedience and conformity to drop dramatically. You could be that person. What have you been keeping quiet about?

licoes.t: Fear as a Tool of Control
p: fear as a tool of control
licoes.r: Fear turns off slow thinking and turns on survival mode. Those who are afraid obey, buy and don't ask. That's why fear is the preferred tool of those who want to control.
licoes.a: In Nuremberg in 1946, Hermann Göring told the psychologist Gustave Gilbert that it is easy to drag the people along: just say they are under attack and accuse the pacifists of a lack of patriotism. The record is in the Nuremberg Diary. The same is true of religious, economic, or health fears when they are exaggerated to sell something. Practice: When faced with a frightening message that calls for urgent action, wait a day and check two sources.
licoes.c: For contemplation: John wrote that perfect love throws fear outside. What would you do today if you weren't afraid of anyone's judgment?

licoes.r: Debt can become an invisible prison: the debtor works for interest and loses his freedom of choice. The book of Proverbs says: "The borrower is a slave to the lender".
licoes.a: Basic financial education, no investment advice: compound interest works for those who save and against those who owe. The revolving credit card in Brazil is among the most expensive interest rates in the world. Steps: List all debts, pay the higher-interest ones first, negotiate, and cut the easy credit. Practice: Write down all your installments today and add up how much of your income is already committed.
licoes.c: To reflect: advertising sells today and charges tomorrow. Freedom is also being able to say no to a desire to say yes to your peace.

licoes.r: The ego is the voice that needs to be right, seen and defended. It's an identity program, made up of name, history, opinions and wounds. He's not an enemy. He's a servant who thinks he's a king.
licoes.a: Buddhism teaches anatta, the non-self: what you call the self is a process, not a fixed thing. Neuroscience observes something similar in a brain network connected to thinking about yourself, which is calmed down in meditation. Practice: Observe when you are easily offended or need to win an argument. There's the ego. Just noticing, he's already losing his strength.
licoes.c: To think about: Jesus said that whoever wants to save his life will lose it. Maybe what needs to die is just the image. Who are you without your story?

licoes.t: How to Get Out of the Matrix
p: how to get out of the matrix
licoes.r: Leaving the Matrix isn't denying the world or falling for conspiracy theories, which is just another Matrix. It's about observing one's own mind, questioning the automatic and making conscious choices. The first gate is to notice when you're on autopilot.
licoes.a: In practice: one, turn off the noise, less news and screens; two, examine your inherited beliefs; three, learn to recognize the fear used to control; four, check sources; five, cultivate silence; six, live what you've discovered, with love. Gurdjieff called self-remembering the effort to be present as one acts. Practice: tell me to break the matrix, and I'll guide the journey in seven steps.
licoes.c: To contemplate: there is no final way out. Every day there's a new cave and a new choice. You don't take the red pill once; you take it every morning.

licoes.r: The Bavarian Illuminati really existed: a society founded on May 1, 1776 by Adam Weishaupt, and banned by the Bavarian government between 1784 and 1785. There's no evidence that they survived or that they control the world. Reptilians, flat earth and the myth that vaccines cause autism also have no evidence.
licoes.a: The mechanisms of power that are documented are no secret: concentration of wealth, lobbying, propaganda, campaign finance, debt. It's more useful to know them than to hunt shadows. Conspiracy theories tend to be as addictive as the Matrix itself: they give you an enemy, a sense of being chosen, and no one needs to prove anything. Historical fact: The Protocols of the Elders of Zion, the basis of much conspiracy, was a hoax exposed by The Times in 1921, and it fueled the hatred that led to the Holocaust. Practice: When faced with a theory, ask yourself, what would prove it to be false?
licoes.c: To contemplate: whoever says that only he sees the truth and that everyone else is wrong is using the same technique of the systems he denounces. Discretion applies to both sides.

licoes.r: Spirituality is the living experience of the sacred. Institution is the human organization around it, with rules, hierarchy and money. The two can go together, but they're not the same thing. The problem isn't faith, it's who profits from fear.
licoes.a: Jesus drove out the merchants from the temple and said, in John four, that the hour was coming when true worshipers would worship the Father in spirit and truth, neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. A lot of institutions do real good, hospitals, schools, charities. The warning sign is when the institution puts itself in God's place. Practice: ask yourself, does my practice make me more free and loving, or more fearful and dependent?
licoes.c: To ponder: If all the churches closed tomorrow, would their connection to the sacred continue? What's yours and what's borrowed?

licoes.r: Indulgence was the reduction of the penalty for sins in purgatory granted by the Church. In the early sixteenth century, it was sold en masse, also to finance St. Peter's Basilica. On October 31, 1517, Martin Luther published the 95 Theses against this trade, and the Reformation began.
licoes.a: The preacher Johann Tetzel is credited with the rhyme: When the coin in the box ticks, the soul in purgatory jumps. Luther replied in thesis 27 that this was a human doctrine. Fact: The Church itself, at the Council of Trent, banned the sellers of indulgences in 1562. Inside reading: forgiveness bought is fear managed. Practice: ask every spiritual promise, does it ask for my money or my transformation?
licoes.c: To contemplate: in Acts 8, Peter says to Simon, who tried to buy the gift of the Spirit: "May your money perish with you, because you thought to buy the gift of God with money". Say Pandora's box to see the techniques that still repeat it today.

licoes.t: Religion in the Service of Power
p: religion in the service of power
licoes.r: Throughout history, religion has often been used to justify power, war, and colonization. Papal bulls of 1452 and 1493 authorized kings to take lands and enslave non-Christian peoples. Beginning in 1513, the Spanish read the Requerimiento to the natives, a requirement that they submit to the church and the king before attacking.
licoes.a: The other side is also true: Friar Bartolomé de las Casas denounced the massacres of the natives, and Quakers and pastors led the fight against slavery. Inner reading: whenever the sacred is used to dominate, it ceases to be sacred and becomes a tool. In 2023 the Vatican repudiated the doctrine of discovery. Practice: say the crimes of the church to see the historical archive with the sources.
licoes.c: To consider: Jesus said that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, but it is not so among you. Whoever wants to be great must be your servant. Where does spiritual leadership serve, and where does it command?

licoes.r: Prosperity theology teaches that faith and giving bring wealth and health. It was born in the United States, in the Word of Faith movement of the twentieth century, with preachers like Kenneth Hagin and the seed of faith of Oral Roberts, and grew very much in Brazilian Neo-Pentecostalism. This is not true of every evangelical church: many reject it.
licoes.a: The mechanism: tithing becomes exchange, giving to receive, and one who does not prosper is guilty of having little faith. It exploits the believer's own desire. Facts: In Brazil, temples of any denomination have immunity from taxes by the Constitution, Article 150, paragraph six, letter b; and there is an evangelical parliamentary front in Congress. Paul wrote that each one should give as he has resolved in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, and that the love of money is a root of all sorts of injurious things. Practice: If an offer comes with a promise of return, it's business, not faith.
licoes.c: To reflect: Jesus said that you cannot serve God and money, and that the Kingdom of God is within you. Would God need your money? With respect to sincere believers, the question is who charges, not who gives from the heart.

p: how do you know if a church
licoes.r: A manipulative group, religious or not, usually shows these signs: constant guilt and fear; money as proof of faith; a leader who cannot be questioned; isolation from outsiders; prohibition from asking or reading reviews; and a terrible fear of leaving. Steven Hassan put this together in the BITE model: control of behavior, information, thought and emotion.
licoes.a: How do you know? Ask yourself, can I disagree with the leader without being punished? Can I read criticism of the group? Can I leave without losing my family and friends? Where does the money go, and is there accountability? If the answer is no to several, it's a red flag. Robert Lifton, in 1961, described eight criteria of totalitarianism, such as control of the environment, loaded language, and doctrine above the person. Practice: Write down your answers and show them to someone you trust outside the group.
licoes.c: To see: Jesus said, by their fruits ye shall know them. Are the fruits of the group in you more freedom, love and peace, or more fear, guilt and dependency? If you need support, seek a psychologist; in Brazil, the CVV answers on 188. Say Pandora's box to see each technique.

licoes.r: The sacred texts did not fall ready from heaven in a single day: they were written, copied, assembled, and selected over the centuries by human communities. That is a historical fact, and it does not diminish anyone's spiritual worth.
licoes.a: Examples: the Council of Nicaea in 325 did NOT choose the books of the Bible, that is a myth; the canon was gradually formed from the second to the fifth century, and was fixed by the Catholic Church at Trent in 1546. There are lost gospels, the apocrypha, and many were rediscovered in Nag Hammadi, Egypt, in 1945. Practice: Read an entire Gospel at once, like a book, and notice what the text itself says.
licoes.c: To ponder: if men chose the books, is the inspiration in the book alone, or also in those who read with an open heart? Tell the truth about the Bible to go deep with the sources.

licoes.t: The Kingdom of God Is Within You
p: the kingdom of god is within
the kingdom of god is within you
licoes.r: At Luke 17:21, Jesus says: The kingdom of God does not come with visible signs; the kingdom of God is within you. The Greek word entos can be translated as within or among you, and both readings exist. In the Gospel of Thomas, the third statement says: the kingdom is within you and outside of you.
licoes.a: Inside reading: if the Kingdom is inside, no institution owns the door. Meister Eckhart, a 14th-century Catholic mystic, spoke of the ground of the soul where God and the soul are one. St. Augustine said that God is more intimate than my innermost self. Practice: five minutes of silence with your hand on your chest, not asking for anything, just being.
licoes.c: To contemplate: if what you're looking for is inside, why do so many sell the map on the outside? The search ends when the seeker turns around.

licoes.t: Religious Matrix: Guilt, Fear, Anger and Greed
p: religious matrix guilt, fear, anger and greed
licoes.r: The religious matrix spins on four gears. Guilt: you're born in debt and you're never good enough. Fear: hell, curse, and punishment. Anger: an external enemy, us against them. Greed: give to receive, which exploits the desire of one's own faithful. Together, they form a self-feeding cycle.
licoes.a: The cycle: guilt creates the need for forgiveness; fear prevents questioning; anger toward outsiders keeps the group together; the promise of reward keeps giving. Hassan calls it emotional control in the BITE model. Spinoza, in the preface to his 1670 Treatise on Theology and Politics, taught that superstition springs from fear, is sustained by fear, and is fed by it. And Henri Tajfel showed in the 1970s that just dividing people into groups creates favoritism and distrust. Practice: When you feel guilt, fear, anger, or spiritual greed, name the gear.
licoes.c: The antidote is self-knowledge and discernment. Jesus said: "You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free", John 8:32. The faith that sets you free doesn't need the four gears. Say fear of hell or Pandora's box.

licoes.r: Fear of hell works as control because infinite punishment gives infinite power to whoever claims to have the key; because it cannot be verified; and because it creates the problem and sells the solution. Fear turns off thought, and guilt closes the trap: control becomes automatic, from the inside out.
licoes.a: Psychology helps us understand: Kahneman and Tversky showed that fearing loss weighs more heavily than wishing for gain; and Terror Management Theory, based on Ernest Becker's 1973 book Death Denial, shows that fear of death causes us to cling tightly to the group's worldview. History: The Hebrew Sheol was the place of the dead, not of torture; Gehenna was the Valley of Hinnom near Jerusalem; the idea of hell developed over centuries, and Dante painted it in the 14th century. Purgatory and indulgences led to Luther's protest in 1517. Origen, in the third century, hoped for a final restoration of all.
licoes.c: With all respect to the one who believes: John's first letter says, there is no fear in love; perfect love casts out fear, 1 John 4:18. If your faith lives in fear, it can be lived in love. To ponder: Do you love God, or do you fear him? Say Pandora's box to see how fear is used.

p: what s the conclusion of all this
qual a conclusao de tudo isso
licoes.r: The sum of history: Inquisitions with some three to five thousand executions in Spain and over a thousand and one hundred in Portugal; forty to sixty thousand killed in the witch hunt; some two hundred and sixteen thousand victims of clergy abuse in France alone since 1950; thousands of children killed in boarding schools and mothers' and babies' homes. The bottom line: more power, more authority that can't be questioned, more fear, equals abuse.
licoes.a: This formula is not unique to religion: atheist regimes of the 20th century, such as Stalin's, Mao's and the Khmer Rouge, political sects and gurus did the same. And the other side is also true: faith built hospitals, Quakers fought against slavery since 1688, and the Rev. Martin Luther King led the fight for civil rights. The right word for the mechanism: Robert Lifton, in 1961, called it thought reform and totalitarianism; the metaphor is the Matrix, a mind control system; the old name is domination.
licoes.c: The opposite of domination is not disbelief, it's conscience: thinking for yourself, checking, loving without fear. To contemplate, where in your life is power, unquestioned authority and fear combined? There is your Matrix. Say break the matrix.

p: hermes trismegistus, commonly known as the hermes hermes
licoes.r: Hermes Trismegistus, the three times greater, is a legendary figure, the fusion of the Greek god Hermes with the Egyptian Thoth. There's no proof that he ever existed as a person. The texts attributed to him, the Corpus Hermeticum, were written in Greek in Roman Egypt around the second and third centuries.
licoes.a: In the Renaissance, Marsilio Ficino translated the Corpus in 1463 thinking it was older than Moses. In 1614, Isaac Casaubon showed by language that it was from the Christian era. Inner reading: Hermes is the messenger between the worlds, the mind that connects high and low. Practice: read the Emerald Tablet and think of a bridge between your inside and your outside.
licoes.c: To contemplate: perhaps Hermes never existed, and yet his image has guided seekers for centuries. Does a symbol have to be historical to be true on the inside?

licoes.r: Pythagoras of Samos lived in the sixth century B.C.E. and founded in Crotona, southern Italy, a community of study, dance, music, and discipline. He left nothing written; almost everything we know came from his disciples and much later authors.
licoes.a: The Pythagoreans taught that number is the essence of things and that the stars produce a harmony of the spheres. The theorem that bears his name was already known to the Babylonians. Inner reading: the order of the cosmos and the order of the soul correspond. Practice: end the day like the Pythagoreans, according to tradition, reviewing what you did, what you didn't do, and where you went wrong.
licoes.c: To contemplate: between chaos and order there is proportion. What proportion is missing in your life today between work and rest, talking and listening?

licoes.r: Heraclitus of Ephesus lived about 500 B.C. He taught that everything is changing, that opposites unite, and that there is a Logos, a reason that governs everything. Only fragments of his work remain.
licoes.a: Fragments known: one cannot step twice into the same river; the way up and down is one; the character of man is his destiny. He was called the Dark One because he spoke in riddles. Practice: today, when something changes against your will, say, the river is different, and so am I.
licoes.c: For contemplation: Heraclitus said that nature loves to hide. What's the truest thing about you that's still hidden?

p: i just know i don t know anything
licoes.r: Socrates of Athens died in 399 B.C.E., condemned to drink hemlock for corrupting youth and failing to honor the city's gods. He wrote nothing; we know him as Plato and Xenophon.
licoes.a: His method was to ask until the person saw the contradictions of one's own certainties: the maiutic, the birth of ideas. In Apology, he says that a life without examination is not worth living. The phrase I only know that I know nothing is a popular summary; Plato writes that he claimed to be wise only because he knew that he did not know. Practice: pick one certainty and give it three why's.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Socrates would rather die than stop asking. What question are you afraid to ask?

licoes.r: Plato, a disciple of Socrates, founded the Academy of Athens about 387 B.C.E. He taught that the world we see is a shadow of a world of eternal Ideas, and that the soul remembers the truth.
licoes.a: The Allegory of the Cave in Book Seven of the Republic sums it all up. For Plato, philosophy is born of awe and is a preparation for death, that is, a detachment from what passes. Practice: Today, in front of something beautiful, ask yourself, what greater beauty is this reflection of?
licoes.c: To contemplate: if the soul remembers, learning is remembering. What do you already know and forget? Say allegory of the cave.

licoes.r: Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, which means awakened, lived in northern India around the fifth century B.C. He taught the Four Noble Truths: there is suffering; it has a cause, attachment; it can cease; and there is a path, the Noble Eightfold Path.
licoes.a: The middle way avoids both excessive pleasure and mortification. The Dhammapada begins like this: the mind precedes all things. And teach: hatred never ceases by hatred; only by love does it cease. Beware: many Buddha quotes on the Internet are false. Practice: Watch your breathing for ten minutes.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Buddha told his disciples that teaching is like a raft, it's for crossing the river, not carrying on your back. What raft are you carrying without needing to?

licoes.r: Lao-tse, the old master, is the sage to whom the Tao Te Ching is attributed. According to legend, he left China riding a buffalo and wrote the book at the request of a border guard. Historians do not know whether he existed as a person; the book seems to have been compiled in the fourth century before Christ.
licoes.a: The central teaching: to live in harmony with the Tao, with simplicity, humility and effortless action. Chapter sixty-four: the journey of a thousand leagues begins beneath your feet. Practice: Do something today that's slower than usual, with full concentration.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the wise man, says the Tao, does not show himself and therefore shines. Where could you shine less to illuminate more? Say the Tao Te Ching.

licoes.r: Most historians, believers and nonbelievers, agree that Jesus of Nazareth existed, was a Jewish preacher from Galilee, and was crucified in Jerusalem under Pontius Pilate about 30 C.E. The center of his teaching is God's Kingdom and love for God and neighbor, even the enemy.
licoes.a: In the Sermon on the Mount, in Matthew five to seven: Blessed are the meek, the merciful, the pure in heart; pray in secret; do not lay up treasures on earth. He denounced those who laid heavy burdens on the shoulders of others and challenged the religious hypocrisy of his day. Practice: Choose a bliss and live it today.
licoes.c: To reflect: At Luke 17:21, the Kingdom of God is within you. If he's in, what needs to come out for him to show up?

licoes.r: Jalal ad-Din Rumi, Persian poet and Sufi master, lived from 1207 to 1273 in Konya, in modern-day Turkey. His encounter with the wandering mystic Shams of Tabriz turned him into a poet of divine love. His greatest work is the Masnavi.
licoes.a: The Masnavi opens with the reed flute that weeps the separation from the reedbed: the soul that yearns for its origin. His followers founded the Mevlevi order, the spinning dervishes. Beware: many of Rumi's phrases circulating on the Internet have been invented or heavily altered, and some erase their Islamic roots. Practice: Listen to a song in complete silence, with your eyes closed, as if it were a prayer.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Rumi called love the astrolabe of the mysteries of God. What in your life do you know just because you loved?

licoes.r: Master Eckhart, a German Dominican friar, lived from about 1260 to 1328. He was one of the greatest Christian mystics. Some of his phrases were condemned by Pope John XXII in 1329, after his death.
licoes.a: He spoke of the depths of the soul, where God gives birth to the Son, and of detachment, the Gelassenheit, letting go. A real phrase from a sermon: The eye with which I see God is the same eye with which God sees me. Practice: For five minutes, stop asking and just stay.
licoes.c: To contemplate: Eckhart prayed to God to rid him of God, that is, of the little images we make of him. What image of God do you need to let go?

licoes.r: Carl Gustav Jung, Swiss psychiatrist, lived from 1875 to 1961. He broke with Freud and created analytical psychology, with ideas like the collective unconscious, archetypes, shadow and individuation, the process of becoming whole.
licoes.a: Jung studied alchemy, gnosticism, myths and religions as maps of the soul. In a 1916 letter, he wrote: "He who looks outside dreams; he who looks within awakens". And in Alchemical Studies, no one becomes enlightened by imagining figures of light, but by making darkness conscious. Practice: Write down one dream a day for a week.
licoes.c: To contemplate: What you most criticize in others may be your shadow. Say shadow to go deeper.

p: the truth and a land without roads
a verdade e uma terra sem caminhos
licoes.r: Jiddu Krishnamurti, an Indian, lived from 1895 to 1986. He was created by the Theosophical Society to be the new teacher of the world, but in 1929 he dissolved the order created for him and said: truth is a pathless land.
licoes.a: He refused to be a guru and taught nonjudgmental observation, freedom from all spiritual authority, including his own. A famous phrase attributed to him, that it is not a sign of health to be adapted to a sick society, has no confirmed source in his works. Practice: observe a thought without condemning or justifying it.
licoes.c: To contemplate: he left the throne given to him so as not to imprison anyone. What authority, even spiritual, have you placed above your own observation?

licoes.r: Ouroboros is the snake, or dragon, that bites its own tail. It appears in ancient Egypt, in a funerary text from the tomb of Tutankhamun, and later in Greek alchemical manuscripts.
licoes.a: It means the eternal cycle: the end that becomes the beginning, the unity of all. In alchemy, it accompanied the Greek phrase one is the whole. Jung saw in him the image of the process of self-transformation. Practice: Observe a cycle of yours that repeats itself, and ask what it wants to teach.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the snake feeds on itself. What part of you needs to be digested to be reborn?

licoes.r: The Eye of Horus, the udjat, is an Egyptian amulet of protection, healing and wholeness. In the myth, Horus loses his eye fighting Seth, and the god Thoth restores it.
licoes.a: Not to be confused: The Eye of Providence, the eye within a triangle of rays, is a Christian symbol of the Trinity and divine watchfulness, appearing on the reverse of the one-dollar bill since 1935 and on the Great Seal of the United States since 1782. He's not a symbol of the Illuminati; that's myth. Practice: Remember today something wounded in you that has already been restored.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the restored eye is worth more than the intact eye, because it knows loss. Which of your wounds became vision?

licoes.r: The Flower of Life is a pattern of equal circles that overlap in six-sided symmetry. It's an ancient geometric figure found in many cultures, and Leonardo da Vinci drew it in his notebooks.
licoes.a: Honesty: There are drawings of her in the temple of Osiris in Abydos, Egypt, but they're probably much more recent than the temple. The idea that it contains all the knowledge of the universe comes from New Age authors like Drunvalo Melchizedek in the 1990's; it's belief, not fact. The geometry itself is beautiful and real. Practice: draw it with a beat, slowly; it's a meditation.
licoes.c: To contemplate: each circle is born from the center of another. Who was the center of where you were born, and whose center are you?

licoes.r: The yin-yang, or taijitu, is the Chinese symbol of two complementary forces: yin, the dark, receptive, cold; yang, the light, active, warm. The design we know became popular from the Song dynasty, around the 11th century.
licoes.a: The essential point is the two dots: there is a little bit of yang in yin and a little bit of yin in yang. Nothing is pure; everything turns into its opposite. Practice: when you're at an extreme today, look for the seed of the opposite within him.
licoes.c: To contemplate: light and shadow are not enemies, they are dance partners. Where are you fighting a half of yourself?

licoes.r: The Tree of Life appears in many cultures: in the Garden of Eden, in Genesis; as Yggdrasil, the Norse world tree; in Kabbalah, with the ten sefirot; and in cultures of Mesopotamia.
licoes.a: It connects three worlds: the roots in the subterranean, the trunk in the earth, the top in the sky. It's the axis of the world, where you go up and down in consciousness. In Revelation, the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations. Practice: Put your feet on the ground barefoot for five minutes, feeling the roots.
licoes.c: To contemplate: no tree grows upward without growing downward in equal measure. Jung remembered something like that about the soul. Do you take care of your roots?

licoes.r: The circumpoint, a circle with a point in the center, is one of the oldest symbols of the Sun. In Egypt it was the hieroglyph of Ra; in astronomy and alchemy it represents the Sun and gold.
licoes.a: Inner reading: the point is consciousness; the circle is the world it illuminates. The sun was honored as a symbol of the divine by Egyptians, Greeks, Incas and many others. Plato compared the idea of Good to the sun, which gives light to see and life to grow. Practice: At dawn, look at the light, never directly at the sun, and say thank you.
licoes.c: To behold: the sun gives light without choosing whom. That's why the Solar Master has that name. What light do you give for free?

licoes.r: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built around 2560 BC for Pharaoh Cheops. Archaeological evidence shows that it was made by organized Egyptian workers housed in villages near the site, not by slaves or extraterrestrials.
licoes.a: Findings such as Merer's diary, papyri more than four thousand five hundred years old, record the transportation of limestone blocks. Symbolic reading: the pyramid is the primordial mountain, the ascent of matter into the sky, the broad base and the unique apex. Practice: Think of your life as a pyramid: What base supports its highest point?
licoes.c: To contemplate: the truth about the pyramids is more impressive than the myth: human beings, with ropes, ramps and organization, touched the sky. Why do we prefer to believe we couldn't?

licoes.r: The lotus flower rises in the mud and blooms clean above the water. So in Hinduism and Buddhism, she is the symbol of purity and awakening in the midst of the world. In Egypt, the blue lotus symbolized the rebirth of the sun.
licoes.a: Fun fact: The lotus leaf repels water and dirt by a microstructure called the lotus effect, which has been studied by science. In the Bhagavad Gita, one who acts without attachment is likened to a lotus leaf that does not get wet. Practice: in the face of a harsh environment today, remember the lotus: to be there without staining.
licoes.c: To contemplate: without mud, there is no lotus. What mud of your history has fed your flower?

licoes.r: The caduceus is the staff of Hermes, with two coiled snakes and wings on top. It's a symbol of the messenger, of trade and reconciliation of opposites.
licoes.a: Fact: The correct symbol of medicine is the staff of Asclepius, with a single snake and no wings. Confusion with the caduceus spread in the United States from 1902 when the U.S. Army adopted it. In esoteric reading, the two snakes are reminiscent of energies rising up the spine, as in yoga, to consciousness above. Practice: Breathe alternately through the nostrils for two minutes, balancing the two forces.
licoes.c: To contemplate: two snakes that could fight climb up together. What two forces in you could stop fighting and rise?

licoes.r: Mandala is Sanskrit for circle. In Hinduism and Buddhism it is a diagram of the cosmos and the spiritual path. Tibetan monks make sand mandalas for days and then undo them.
licoes.a: Jung observed that his patients drew mandalas spontaneously in phases of inner reorganization, and he saw them as symbols of the Self, the center of the whole. He himself drew one a day around 1918. Practice: Draw a circle and fill it out without planning, starting in the center.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the monks undo the mandala to teach impermanence. Can you create something beautiful and let it go?

licoes.r: For Jung, the shadow is the part of us that we don't accept and hide from ourselves: anger, envy, desires, but also rejected talents. What we don't look at, we project onto others.
licoes.a: Jung wrote, in Alchemical Studies: no one becomes enlightened by imagining figures of light, but by making darkness conscious. Integrating the shadow is not obeying it, it's recognizing it so it doesn't act in hiding. Practice: Write down the name of someone who irritates you the most and the quality that irritates him. Then ask, where does that live in me?
licoes.c: To contemplate: Spirituality that wants only light often hides a lot of shadow. What part of you was exiled to make you look good?

licoes.r: Archetypes, for Jung, are universal patterns of the psyche that appear in myths, dreams and religions around the world: the hero, the great mother, the wise old man, the cheater, the divine child.
licoes.a: Joseph Campbell, in The Hero of a Thousand Faces, 1949, showed the hero's journey repeated in many myths: the call, the refusal, the mentor, the crossing, the ordeal, the return with the elixir. It is an influential theory, not a law; critics point out that it simplifies the diversity of cultures. Practice: At what stage of the journey are you now?
licoes.c: To reflect: When an archetype possesses us, we act without realizing it, like the saviour who runs out of energy or the rebel who always fights. What archetype is guiding your life today?

licoes.r: Jung proposed that, in addition to the personal unconscious, there is a collective unconscious, common to all of humanity, from which archetypes would come. It's an influential hypothesis in psychology and religious studies, but it's not proven by experimental science.
licoes.a: Freud saw the unconscious above all as a repository of the repressed; Jung, also as a creative and religious source. Current neuroscience confirms that most mental processing takes place outside of consciousness, but this is different from Jungian theory. Practice: Before you go to sleep, ask your unconscious a question, and write down what comes up when you wake up.
licoes.c: To contemplate: if we are islands, the unconscious would be the bottom of the sea that unites us. What do you feel comes from further away than your own story?

licoes.r: Science knows that we dream mostly in REM sleep, several times a night, and that sleep helps consolidate memories and regulate emotions. Exactly why we dream is still unknown; there are several hypotheses.
licoes.a: Symbolic reading: Freud called the dream the via regia to the unconscious; Jung saw in it a compensation, showing what the consciousness ignores. For Jung, the dream speaks of the dreamer: each character can be a part of you. Be wary of dream dictionaries with fixed meanings; the symbol depends on your life. Practice: Leave a piece of paper by your bed and write down your dream before you get up.
licoes.c: To contemplate: the Upanishads describe waking, dreaming and deep sleep, and a fourth state, the witness that remains in the three. Who are you when you're not dreaming or awake?

licoes.r: Lucid dreaming is realizing you're dreaming inside the dream. It's been proven in the lab: in the 1970s, Keith Hearne, and in 1980, Stephen LaBerge, showed lucid dreamers sending combined signals with their eyes during REM sleep.
licoes.a: Techniques studied: reality tests during the day, asking am I dreaming?; the dream diary; and waking up in the morning and going back to sleep with the intention of realizing. Tibetan Buddhism has an ancient practice, dream yoga. Astral projection, as an actual exit from the body, has no scientific proof. Practice: five times today, look at your hands and ask, am I dreaming?
licoes.c: For contemplation: Tibetan masters say that one who awakens in a dream learns to awaken in life. How many hours of your day do you spend daydreaming without knowing it?

licoes.r: Synchronicity is the name Carl Jung gave to meaningful coincidences: seeing 11:11, thinking about someone and the person calling. He wrote about it in a 1952 essay with the physicist Wolfgang Pauli.
licoes.a: Science explains much of this by the confirmation bias: we notice what matches and forget the rest, and improbable coincidences are expected in a world of billions of events. Jung told the story of the golden beetle that hit the window while a patient was recounting a dream about a beetle. Practice: When you notice a sign, ask yourself, What good decision does it remind me to make? And use it wisely.
licoes.c: To contemplate: meaning is not hidden in things; it is born in the encounter between you and them. What would you do with a sign if you knew it was just a mirror?

licoes.r: How it works: You're taught that you're born in debt and you're never good enough. Guilt becomes permanent, and forgiveness only comes through the institution. Example: sermons that remind you every week how unworthy you are, without ever announcing peace.
licoes.a: How to recognize: You feel guilty even for thinking, for resting, for having fun, and for relief only when you do what the group tells you to do. Lifton called it a requirement of purity and cult of confession. Note that the prophet Ezekiel already said, in chapter 18: the son shall not bear the guilt of the father.
licoes.c: How to free yourself: separate the healthy guilt, which points to a real mistake and asks for redress, from the toxic guilt, which accuses your being. Paul wrote, in Romans eight: there is no condemnation. To contemplate: Whose voice is accusing you inside?

licoes.r: How it works: Threatened with hell, curse or disgrace to anyone who disobeys, doubts, leaves or doesn't hurt. Example: If you leave the church, your family will be cursed.
licoes.a: How to recognize: the threat cannot be verified, but the fear is real and immediate; and the threat is the one that offers protection. It's the problem and solution pair. Say fear of hell to see the full story of that idea.
licoes.c: How to break free: remember that love does not threaten. 1 John 4:18: perfect love throws out fear. To ponder: Would a God of love need a threat to be loved?

licoes.t: The Terror of the End Times
p: date of the end of the world
the terror of the end times
licoes.r: How it works: Announce that the end is near, sometimes with a date set, to create urgency: sell everything, donate everything, obey now. Historical example: The preacher William Miller dated Christ's return to 1844; it did not happen, and the episode became known as the Great Deception. Harold Camping set it for 2011.
licoes.a: How to recognize: urgency, date, request for money or break up with family. Jesus said, at Matthew 24:36, of that day and hour no one knows. And Deuteronomy, chapter eighteen, verse twenty-two, teaches that if what the prophet says does not come to pass, he has spoken presumptuously.
licoes.c: How to break free: No big decision is made in a hurry. Wait, check with people on the outside, check the same leader's past prophecies. To ponder: If the world ended tomorrow, would you still choose to live in fear today?

licoes.r: How it works: The donation is presented as an investment with a guaranteed return: sow to reap, make a pact, give what you don't have. Example: campaigns that promise healing, employment, or marriage in exchange for a high-value offer.
licoes.a: How to recognize: there is the promise of material return, public pressure, suggested values and blame for failure. Robert Cialdini described reciprocity as one of the principles of persuasion: whoever receives something feels obligated to give back, and here it reverses, you give expecting God to be obligated. But Paul wrote, at 2 Corinthians 9, that each one should give as he has resolved in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion.
licoes.c: How to free yourself: Give, if you will, out of gratitude and accountability, never as a purchase. In Acts 8, Peter rebukes those who wanted to buy God's gift. To ponder: Would God need money?

licoes.r: How it works: You're taught that you're only protected under the umbrella of the leader, and that disobeying him is disobeying God. Example: needing permission from the pastor to get married, change jobs or town.
licoes.a: How to recognize: The leader decides over his personal life, is not accountable, and treats any question as rebellion. In the BITE model, it's behavior control. Milgram showed how ordinary people obey authority even against their conscience.
licoes.c: How to break free: Remember Matthew 23: One is your teacher, and you are all brothers; and from Mark 10: whoever wants to be great must be your servant. Healthy leadership accepts being questioned. To contemplate: who covers the leader?

p: don t touch the anointed one
you can t criticize the pastor
licoes.r: How it works: Psalm 105 is used, verse 15, "Touch not my anointed", to prohibit any criticism of the leader. For example, one who reports an abuse is accused of touching the anointed and threatened with punishment.
licoes.a: How to recognize: Read the context. In verses nine to fifteen, the psalm speaks of the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, protected from foreign kings. In the story of David and Saul, in 1 Samuel 24, not touching is not physically hurting, and not forbidding speech. The prophet Nathan confronted King David about his sin, as recorded at 2 Samuel 12.
licoes.c: How to break free: The Beroeans, at Acts 17:11, examined the Scriptures to see if what Paul said was true, and they were commended for it. True criticism is not attacking. To ponder, why would a man of God fear being examined?

licoes.r: How it works: Doubt is called enemy attack, lack of faith, or rebellion. So one becomes a policeman of one's own mind. Example: that's the devil putting thoughts in your head.
licoes.a: How to recognize: You're afraid to think about certain questions. Lifton called sacred science, the doctrine that cannot be questioned, and loaded language, the clichés that enclose thought. In the BITE model, it's thought control.
licoes.c: How to break free: Paul wrote, examine all things and hold fast to what is fine, 1 Thessalonians 5:21, and John, prove the spirits, 1 John 4:1. A truth is not afraid of questions. To reflect: How would you know if you were wrong?

p: they re friends of the church
don t mix with the world
nao se misture com o mundo
licoes.r: How it works: It teaches that the world outside is the devil's, that the unbelieving family is the enemy, and that only the group is safe. Example: discouraging friendships, studies, and programs outside the church.
licoes.a: How to recognize: your whole social life is inside the group, you only get information from it and you're afraid of people outside. Lifton called it environmental control, and the BITE model information control.
licoes.c: How to break free: Build bridges, little by little, with family and friends outside. Jesus ate with publicans and sinners. To ponder: Would a group that has the truth need to hide you from the world?

licoes.r: How it works: On arrival, the person receives undue attention, praise, and affection, and finally feels loved. Then that love becomes conditional on obedience. The term love bombing was used in the 1970's in connection with the Unification Church, and today it applies to cults and abusive relationships.
licoes.a: How to recognize: too much intensity too soon, too much haste for you to commit, and a sudden coldness when you disagree or fail. Cialdini described affection: we say yes to whom we like.
licoes.c: How to break free: True love doesn't change when you disagree. Notice what happens the day you say no. To contemplate: Is this affection for you, or for what you can give to the group?

licoes.r: How it works: Anyone who errs or disagrees is exposed in front of everyone, removed from office or banned from participating. The fear of shame keeps the rest in line. Example: announcing from the pulpit the name of the one who is in discipline.
